1.1: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
1.2: And the earth was without form and void, and darkenesse was upon the deep, and the Spirit of God mooued upon the waters.
1.3: Then God said, Let there be light: And there was light.
1.4: And God saw the light that it was good, and God separated the light from the darkenes.
1.5: And God called the Light, Day, and the darkenes, he called Night. So the evening and the morning were the first day.
1.6: Again God said, Let there be a firmament in the mids of the waters: and let it separate the waters from the waters.
1.7: Then God made the firmament, and separated the waters, which were under the firmament, from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.
1.8: And God called the firmament Heaven. So the Evening and the morning were the second day.
1.9: God said again, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear. and it was so.
1.10: And God called the dry land, Earth, and he called the gathering together of the waters, Seas: and God saw that it was good.
1.11: Then God said, Let the earth bud forth the bud of the herb, that seedeth seed, the fruitful tree, which beareth fruit according to his kind, which hath his seed in it self upon the earth: and it was so.
1.12: And the earth brought foorth the bud of the herb, that seedeth seed according to his kind, also the tree that beareth fruit, which hath his seed in it self according to his kind: and God saw that it was good.
1.13: So the evening and the morning were the third day.
1.14: And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven, to separate the day from the night, and let them be for signes, and for seasons, and for dayes and yeeres.
1.15: And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so.
1.16: God then made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the less light to rule the night: he made also the starres.
1.17: And God set them in the firmament of the heaven, to shine upon the earth,
1.18: And to rule in the day, and in the night, and to separate the light from the darkenesse: and God saw that it was good.
1.19: So the evening and the morning were the fourth day.
1.20: Afterward God said, Let the waters bring foorth in abundance every creeping thing that hath life: and let the fowl flie upon the earth in the open firmament of the heaven.
1.21: Then God created the great whales, and every thing living and moving, which the waters brought foorth in abundance according to their kind, and every fethered fowl according to his kind: and God saw that it was good.
1.22: Then God blessed them, saying, Bring foorth fruit and multiplie, and fill the waters in the seas, and let the fowl multiplie in the earth.
1.23: So the evening and the morning were the fifte day.
1.24: Moreover God said, Let the earth bring foorth the living thing according to his kind, cattel, and that which creepeth, and the beast of the earth, according to his kind. and it was so.
1.25: And God made the beast of the earth according to his kind, and the cattell according to his kind, and every creeping thing of the earth according to his kind: and God saw that it was good.
1.26: Furthermore God said, Let us make man in our image according to our likenes, and let them rule over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the heaven, and over the beastes, and over all the earth, and over every thing that creepeth and moveth on the earth.
1.27: Thus God created the man in his image: in the image of God created he him: he created them male and female.
1.28: And God blessed them, and God said to them, Bring forth fruit and multiplie, and fill the earth, and subdue it, and rule over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the heaven, and over every beast that moveth upon the earth.
1.29: And God said, Behold, I have given unto you every herb bearing seed, which is upon al the earth, and every tree, wherein is the fruit of a tree bearing seed: that shall be to you for meat.
1.30: Likewise to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the heaven, and to every thing that moveth upon the earth, which hath life in it self, every green herb shall be for meat. and it was so.
1.31: And God saw all that he had made, and loe, it was very good. So the evening and the morning were the sixt day.

2.1: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.
2.2: For in the seventh day GOD ended his work which he had made, and the seventh day he rested from al his work, which he had made.
2.3: So God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it, because that in it he had rested from all his work, which God had created and made.
2.4: These are the generations of the heavens and of the earth, when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made the earth and the heavens,
2.5: And every plant of the field, before it was in the earth, and every herb of the field, before it grew: for the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, neither was there a man to till the ground,
2.6: But a myst went up from the earth, and watered all the earth.
2.7: The Lord God also made the man of the dust of the ground, and breathed in his face breath of life, and the man was a living soul.
2.8: And the Lord God planted a garden Eastward in Eden, and there he put the man whom he had made.
2.9: (For out of the ground made the Lord God to grow every tree pleasant to the sight, and good for meat: the tree of life also in the mids of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and of evil.
2.10: And out of Eden went a river to water the garden, and from thence it was deuided, and became into four heads.
2.11: The name of one is Pishon: the same compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where is gold.
2.12: And the gold of that land is good: there is Bdelium, and the Onix stone.
2.13: And the name of the second river is Gihon: the same compasseth the whole land of Cush.
2.14: The name also of the third river is Hiddekel: this goeth toward the Eastside of Asshur: and the fourth river is Perath)
2.15: Then the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden, that he might dress it and keep it.
2.16: And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Thou shalt eat freely of every tree of the garden,
2.17: But of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof, thou shalt die the death.
2.18: Also the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be himself alone: I wil make him an help meet for him.
2.19: So the Lord God formed of the earth every beast of the field, and every fowl of the heaven, and brought them unto the man to see how he would call them: for howsoever the man named the living creature, so was the name thereof.
2.20: The man therefore gave names unto all cattell, and to the fowl of the heaven, and to every beast of the field: but for Adam found he not an help meet for him.
2.21: Therefore the Lord God caused an heauie sleep to fall upon the man, and he slept: and he took one of his ribbes, and closed up the flesh in stead thereof.
2.22: And the ribbe which the Lord God had taken from the man, made he a woman, and brought her to the man.
2.23: Then the man said, This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh. She shalbe called woman, because she was taken out of man.
2.24: Therefore shall man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they shall be one flesh.
2.25: And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.

3.1: Now the serpent was more subtil then any beast of the field, which the Lord God had made: and he said to the woman, Yea, hath God in deed said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
3.2: And the woman said unto the serpent, We eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden,
3.3: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the middes of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.
3.4: Then the serpent said to the woman, Ye shall not die at all,
3.5: But God doeth know, that when ye shall eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.
3.6: So the woman (seeing that the tree was good for meat, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to get knowledge) took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also to her husband with her, and he did eat.
3.7: Then the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they sewed figge tree leaves together, and made them selves breeches.
3.8: Afterward they heard the voyce of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God among the trees of the garden.
3.9: But the Lord God called to the man, and said unto him, Where art thou?
3.10: Who said, I heard thy voyce in the garden, and was afraid: because I was naked, therefore I hid my self.
3.11: And he said, Who told thee, that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?
3.12: Then the man said, The woman which thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.
3.13: And the Lord God said to the woman, Why hast thou done this? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.
3.14: Then the Lord God said to the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattell, and above every beast of the field: upon thy belly shalt thou goe, and dust shalt thou eat all the dayes of thy life.
3.15: I will also put enimitie between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed. He shall break thine head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
3.16: Unto the woman he said, I will greatly increase thy sorowes, and thy conceptions. In sorowe shalt thou bring foorth children, and thy desire shalbe subiect to thine husband, and he shall rule over thee.
3.17: Also to Adam he said, Because thou hast obeyed the voyce of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, (whereof I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it) cursed is the earth for thy sake: in sorowe shalt thou eat of it all the dayes of thy life.
3.18: Thornes also, and thistles shall it bring foorth to thee, and thou shalt eat the herb of the field.
3.19: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return to the earth: for out of it wast thou taken, because thou art dust, and to dust shalt thou return.
3.20: (And the man called his wives name Heuah, because she was the mother of all living)
3.21: Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coates of skinnes, and clothed them.
3.22: And the Lord God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil. And now lest he put foorth his hand, and take also of ye tree of life and eat and live for ever,
3.23: Therefore the Lord God sent him foorth from the garden of Eden, to till ye earth, whence he was taken.
3.24: Thus he cast out man, and at the East side of the garden of Eden he set the Cherubims, and the blade of a sword shaken, to keep the way of the tree of life.

4.1: Afterward the man knew Heuah his wife, which conceived and bare Kain, and said, I have obteined a man by the Lord.
4.2: And again she brought foorth his brother Habel, and Habel was a keeper of sheep, and Kain was a tiller of the ground.
4.3: And in process of time it came to pass, that Kain brought an oblation unto the Lord of the fruit of the ground.
4.4: And Habel also him self brought of the first fruites of his sheep, and of the fat of them, and the Lord had respect unto Habel, and to his offering,
4.5: But unto Kain and to his offering he had no regard: wherefore Kain was exceeding wroth, and his countenance fell down.
4.6: Then ye Lord said unto Kain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance cast down?
4.7: If thou do well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sinne lieth at the door: also unto thee his desire shalbe subiect, and thou shalt rule over him.
4.8: Then Kain spake to Habel his brother. And when they were in the field, Kain rose up against Habel his brother, and slew him.
4.9: Then the Lord said unto Kain, Where is Habel thy brother? Who answered, I cannot tell. Am I my brothers keeper?
4.10: Again he said, What hast thou done? the voyce of thy brothers blood cryeth unto me from the earth.
4.11: Now therefore thou art cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brothers blood from thine hand.
4.12: When thou shalt till the ground, it shall not henceforth yeelde unto thee her strength: a vagabond and a runnagate shalt thou be in the earth.
4.13: Then Kain said to the Lord, My punishment is greater, then I can bear.
4.14: Behold, thou hast cast me out this day from the earth, and from thy face shall I be hid, and shalbe a vagabond, and a runnagate in the earth, and whosoever findeth me, shall slay me.
4.15: Then the Lord said unto him, Doubtless whosoever slayeth Kain, he shalbe punished seue fold. And the Lord set a mark upon Kain, lest any man finding him should kill him.
4.16: Then Kain went out from the presence of the Lord, and dwelt in the land of Nod toward the Eastside of Eden.
4.17: Kain also knew his wife, which conceived and bare Henoch: and he built a citie, and called the name of the citie by ye name of his sonne, Henoch.
4.18: And to Henoch was borne Irad, and Irad begat Mehuiael, and Mehuiael begat Methushael, and Methushael begat Lamech.
4.19: And Lamech took him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
4.20: And Adah bare Jabal, who was the father of such as dwell in the tents, and of such as have cattell.
4.21: And his brothers name was Jubal, who was the father of all that play on the harp and organes.
4.22: And Zillah also bare Tubal-kain, who wrought cunningly every craft of brass and of yron: and the sister of Tubal-kain was Naamah.
4.23: Then Lamech said unto his wives Adah and Zillah, Hear my voyce, ye wives of Lamech: hearken unto my speach: for I would slay a man in my wound, and a yong man in mine hurt.
4.24: If Kain shalbe avenged seven fold, truely Lamech, seuentie times seven fold.
4.25: And Adam knew his wife again, and she bare a sonne, and she called his name Sheth: for God, said she, hath appointed me another seed for Habel, because Kain slew him.
4.26: And to ye same Sheth also there was borne a sonne, and he called his name Enosh. Then beganne men to call upon the name of the Lord.

5.1: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created Adam, in the likenes of God made he him,
5.2: Male and female created he them, and blessed them, and called their name Adam in the day that they were created.
5.3: Now Adam lived an hundred and thirtie yeeres, and begat a child in his own likenes after his image, and called his name Sheth.
5.4: And the dayes of Adam, after he had begotten Sheth, were eight hundreth yeeres, and he begat sonnes and daughters.
5.5: So all the dayes that Adam lived, were nine hundreth and thirtie yeeres: and he died.
5.6: And Sheth lived an hundreth and five yeeres, and begat Enosh.
5.7: And Sheth lived, after he begat Enosh, eight hundreth and seven yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
5.8: So all the dayes of Sheth were nine hundreth and twelve yeeres: and he died.
5.9: Also Enosh lived ninetie yeeres, and begat Kenan.
5.10: And Enosh lived, after he begat Kenan, eight hundreth and fifteen yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
5.11: So all the dayes of Enosh were nine hundreth and five yeeres: and he died
5.12: Likewise Kenan lived seuentie yeeres, and begat Mahalaleel.
5.13: And Kenan lived, after he begat Mahalaleel, eight hundreth and fourtie yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
5.14: So all the dayes of Kenan were nine hundreth and tenne yeeres: and he died.
5.15: Mahalaleel also lived sixtie and five yeres, and begat Jered.
5.16: Also Mahalaleel lived, after he begat Jered, eight hundreth and thirtie yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
5.17: So all the dayes of Mahalaleel were eight hundreth ninetie and five yeeres: and he died.
5.18: And Jered lived an hundreth sixtie and two yeeres, and begat Henoch.
5.19: Then Jered lived, after he begat Henoch, eight hundreth yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
5.20: So all the dayes of Jered were nine hundreth sixtie and two yeeres: and he died.
5.21: Also Henoch lived sixtie and five yeeres, and begat Methushelah.
5.22: And Henoch walked with God, after he begat Methushelah, three hundreth yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
5.23: So all the dayes of Henoch were three hundreth sixtie and five yeeres.
5.24: And Henoch walked with God, and he was no more seen: for God took him away.
5.25: Methushelah also lived an hundreth eightie and seven yeeres, and begat Lamech.
5.26: And Methushelah lived, after he begat Lamech, seven hundreth eightie and two yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
5.27: So al the dayes of Methushelah were nine hundreth sixtie and nine yeeres: and he died.
5.28: Then Lamech lived an hundreth eightie and two yeeres, and begat a sonne,
5.29: And called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and sorowe of our hands, as touching the earth, which the Lord hath cursed.
5.30: And Lamech lived, after he begat Noah, five hundreth ninetie and five yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
5.31: So all the dayes of Lamech were seven hundreth seuentie and seven yeeres: and he died.
5.32: And Noah was five hundreth yeere old. And Noah begat Shem, Ham and Japheth.

6.1: So when men began to be multiplied upon the earth, and there were daughters borne unto them,
6.2: Then the sonnes of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair, and they took them wives of all that they liked.
6.3: Therefore the Lord said, My Spirit shall not alway strive with man, because he is but flesh, and his dayes shalbe an hundreth and twentie yeeres.
6.4: There were gyants in the earth in those dayes: yea, and after that the sonnes of God came unto the daughters of men, and they had borne them children, these were mightie men, which in old time were men of renoume.
6.5: When the Lord saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and all the imaginations of the thoughtes of his heart were onely evil continually,
6.6: Then it repented ye Lord, that he had made man in the earth, and he was sorie in his heart.
6.7: Therefore ye Lord said, I will destroy from the earth the man, whom I have created, from man to beast, to the creeping thing, and to the fowl of the heaven: for I repent that I have made them.
6.8: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.
6.9: These are the generations of Noah. Noah was a just and upright man in his time: and Noah walked with God.
6.10: And Noah begat three sonnes, Shem, Ham and Japheth.
6.11: The earth also was corrupt before God: for the earth was filled with crueltie.
6.12: Then God looked upon the earth, and behold, it was corrupt: for all flesh had corrupt his way upon the earth.
6.13: And God said unto Noah, An end of all flesh is come before me: for the earth is filled with crueltie through them: and behold, I wil destroy them with the earth.
6.14: Make thee an Ark of pine trees: thou shalt make cabines in the Ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
6.15: And thus shalt thou make it: The length of the Ark shalbe three hundreth cubites, the breadth of it fiftie cubites, and the height of it thirtie cubites.
6.16: A window shalt thou make in the Ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above, and the door of the Ark shalt thou set in the side thereof: thou shalt make it with the low, second and third roume.
6.17: And I, behold, I will bring a flood of waters upon the earth to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life under the heaven: all that is in the earth shall perish.
6.18: But with thee will I establish my covenant, and thou shalt goe into the Ark, thou, and thy sonnes, and thy wife, and thy sonnes wives with thee.
6.19: And of every living thing, of all flesh two of every sort shalt thou cause to come into the Ark, to keep them alive with thee: they shalbe male and female.
6.20: Of the foules, after their kind, and of the cattell after their kind, of every creeping thing of the earth after his kind, two of every sort shall come unto thee, that thou mayest keep them alive.
6.21: And take thou with thee of all meat that is eaten: and thou shalt gather it to thee, that it may be meat for thee and for them.
6.22: Noah therefore did according unto all, that God commanded him: even so did he.

7.1: And the Lord said unto Noah, Enter thou and all thine house into the Ark: for thee have I seen righteous before me in this age.
7.2: Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee by sevens, the male and his female: but of vncleane beastes by couples, the male and his female.
7.3: Of the foules also of the heaven by sevens, male and female, to keep seed alive upon the whole earth.
7.4: For seven dayes hence I will cause it rain upon the earth fourtie dayes and fourtie nightes, and all the substance that I have made, will I destroy from off the earth.
7.5: Noah therefore did according unto all that the Lord commanded him.
7.6: And Noah was six hundreth yeeres old, when the flood of waters was upon the earth.
7.7: So Noah entred and his sonnes, and his wife, and his sonnes wives with him into the Ark, because of the waters of the flood.
7.8: Of the clean beastes, and of the vncleane beastes, and of the foules, and of all that creepeth upon the earth,
7.9: There came two and two unto Noah into the Ark, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.
7.10: And so after seven dayes the waters of the flood were upon the earth.
7.11: In the six hundreth yeere of Noahs life in the second moneth, the seuetenth day of the moneth, in the same day were all the fountaines of the great deep broken up, and the windowes of heaven were opened,
7.12: And the rain was upon the earth fourtie dayes and fourtie nightes.
7.13: In the self same day entred Noah with Shem, and Ham and Japheth, the sonnes of Noah, and Noahs wife, and the three wives of his sonnes with them into the Ark.
7.14: They and every beast after his kind, and all cattell after their kind, and every thing that creepeth and moveth upon the earth after his kind, and every fowl after his kind, even every bird of every fether.
7.15: For they came to Noah into ye Ark, two and two, of all flesh wherein is ye breath of life.
7.16: And they entring in, came male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him: and the Lord shut him in.
7.17: Then ye flood was fourtie dayes upon the earth, and the waters were increased, and bare up the Ark, which was lift up above the earth.
7.18: The waters also waxed strong, and were increased exceedingly upon the earth, and the Ark went upon the waters.
7.19: The waters prevailed so exceedingly upon the earth, that all the high mountaines, that are under the whole heaven, were covered.
7.20: Fifteen cubites vpwarde did the waters prevail, when the mountaines were covered.
7.21: Then all flesh perished that moved upon the earth, both fowl and cattell and beast, and every thing that creepeth and moveth upon the earth, and every man.
7.22: Every thing in whose nostrels the spirit of life did breathe, whatsoever they were in the drie land, they died.
7.23: So he destroyed every thing that was upon the earth, from man to beast, to ye creeping thing, and to the fowl of the heaven: they were even destroyed from the earth. And Noah onely remained; and they that were with him in ye Ark.
7.24: And the waters prevailed upon the earth an hundreth and fiftie dayes.

8.1: Now God remembred Noah and every beast, and all the cattell that was with him in the Ark: therefore God made a wind to pass upon the earth, and the waters ceased.
8.2: The fountaines also of the deep and the windowes of heaven were stopped and the rain from heaven was restrained,
8.3: And the waters returned from above the earth, going and returning: and after the end of the hundreth and fiftieth day the waters abated.
8.4: And in the seventh moneth, in the seventeenth day of the moneth, the Ark rested upon the mountaines of Ararat.
8.5: And the waters were going and decreasing until the tenth moneth: in the tenth moneth, and in the first day of the moneth were the toppes of the mountaines seen.
8.6: So after fourtie dayes, Noah opened the window of the Ark, which he had made,
8.7: And sent forth a raven, which went out going forth and returning, until the waters were dried up upon the earth.
8.8: Again he sent a dove from him, that he might see if the waters were diminished from off the earth.
8.9: But the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot: therefore she returned unto him into the Ark (for the waters were upon the whole earth) and he put forth his hand, and received her, and took her to him into the Ark.
8.10: And he abode yet other seven dayes, and again he sent forth the dove out of the Ark.
8.11: And the dove came to him in ye evening, and loe, in her mouth was an olive leaf that she had pluckt: whereby Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
8.12: Notwithstanding he wayted yet other seven dayes, and sent forth the dove, which returned not again unto him any more.
8.13: And in the six hundreth and one yeere, in the first day of the first moneth the waters were dryed up from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the Ark and looked, and behold, the upper part of the ground was drie.
8.14: And in the second moneth, in the seven and twentieth day of the moneth was the earth drie.
8.15: Then God spake to Noah, saying,
8.16: Goe forth of the Ark, thou and thy wife, and thy sonnes and thy sonnes wives with thee.
8.17: Bring forth with thee every beast that is with thee, of all flesh, both fowl and cattell, and every thing that creepeth and moveth upon the earth, that they may breed abundantly in ye earth, and bring forth fruit and increase upon ye earth.
8.18: So Noah came forth, and his sonnes, and his wife, and his sonnes wives with him.
8.19: Every beast, every creeping thing, and every fowl, all that moveth upon the earth after their kindes went out of the Ark.
8.20: Then Noah built an altar to the Lord and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and offered burnt offerings upon the altar.
8.21: And the Lord smelled a sauour of rest, and the Lord said in his heart, I will hencefoorth curse the ground no more for mans cause: for the imagination of mans heart is evil, even from his youth: neither will I smite any more all things living, as I have done.
8.22: Hereafter seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and sommer and winter, and day and night shall not cease, so long as ye earth remaineth.

9.1: And God blessed Noah and his sonnes, and said to them, Bring foorth fruit, and multiplie, and replenish the earth.
9.2: Also the fear of you, and the dread of you shalbe upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the heaven, upon all that moveth on the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea: into your hand are they delivered.
9.3: Every thing that moveth and liveth, shall be meat for you: as the green herb, have I given you all things.
9.4: But flesh with the life thereof, I mean, with the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.
9.5: For surely I will require your blood, wherein your lives are: at the hand of every beast will I require it: and at the hand of man, even at the hand of a mans brother will I require the life of man.
9.6: Who so sheadeth mans blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God hath he made man.
9.7: But bring ye forth fruit and multiplie: grow plentifully in the earth, and increase therein.
9.8: God spake also to Noah and to his sonnes with him, saying,
9.9: Behold, I, even I establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you,
9.10: And with every living creature that is with you, with the fowl, with the cattell, and with every beast of the earth with you, from all that goe out of the Ark, unto every beast of the earth.
9.11: And my covenant will I establish with you, that from henceforth all flesh shall not be rooted out by ye waters of the flood, neither shall there be a flood to destroy the earth any more.
9.12: Then God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you, and between every living thing, that is with you unto perpetual generations.
9.13: I have set my bow in the cloud, and it shalbe for a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
9.14: And when I shall cover the earth with a cloud, and the bow shall be seen in the cloud,
9.15: Then will I remember my covenant, which is between me and you, and between every living thing in all flesh, and there shalbe no more waters of a flood to destroy all flesh.
9.16: Therefore the bow shalbe in the cloud, that I may see it, and remember the everlasting covenant between God, and every living thing in all flesh that is upon the earth.
9.17: God said yet to Noah, This is the sign of the covenant, which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.
9.18: Now the sonnes of Noah going foorth of the Ark, were Shem and Ham and Japheth. And Ham is the father of Canaan.
9.19: These are the three sonnes of Noah, and of them was the whole earth ouerspred.
9.20: Noah also began to be an husband man and planted a vineyard.
9.21: And he drunk of ye wine and was drunken, and was vncouered in the middes of his tent.
9.22: And when Ham the father of Canaan saw the nakedness of his father, he told his two brethren without.
9.23: Then took Shem and Japheth a garment, and put it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father with their faces backward: so they saw not their fathers nakedness.
9.24: Then Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his yonger sonne had done unto him,
9.25: And said, Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.
9.26: He said moreover, blessed be the Lord God of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant.
9.27: God perswade Japheth, that he may dwell in the tentes of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant.
9.28: And Noah lived after the flood three hundreth and fiftie yeeres.
9.29: So all the dayes of Noah were nine hundreth and fiftie yeeres: and he died.

10.1: Now these are the generations of the sonnes of Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth: unto whom sonnes were borne after the flood.
10.2: The sonnes of Japheth were Gomer and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
10.3: And the sonnes of Gomer, Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
10.4: Also the sonnes of Javan, Elishah and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
10.5: Of these were the yles of the Gentiles deuided in their landes, every man after his tongue, and after their families in their nations.
10.6: Moreover, ye sonnes of Ham were Cush, and Mizraim, and Put, and Canaan.
10.7: And the sonnes of Cush, Seba and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtecha: also the sonnes of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
10.8: And Cush begat Nimrod, who began to be mightie in the earth.
10.9: He was a mightie hunter before the Lord. wherefore it is said, As Nimrod the mightie hunter before the Lord.
10.10: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
10.11: Out of that land came Asshur, and builded Niniueh, and the citie Rehoboth, and Calah:
10.12: Resen also between Niniueh and Calah: this is a great citie.
10.13: And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim.
10.14: Pathrusim also, and Casluhim (out of whom came the Philistims) and Caphtorims.
10.15: Also Canaan begat Zidon his first borne, and Heth,
10.16: And Jebusi, and Emori, and Girgashi,
10.17: And Hiui, and Arki, and Sini,
10.18: And Aruadi, and Zemari, and Hamathi: and afterward were the families of the Canaanites spred abroad.
10.19: Then the border of the Canaanites was from Zidon, as thou comest to Gerar until Azzah, and as thou goest unto Sodom, and Gomorah, and Admah, and Zeboijm, even unto Lasha.
10.20: These are the sonnes of Ham according to their families, according to their tongues in their countries and in their nations.
10.21: Unto Shem also the father of all the sonnes of Eber, and elder brother of Japheth were children borne.
10.22: The sonnes of Shem were Elam and Asshur, and Arpachshad, and Lud, and Aram.
10.23: And the sonnes of Aram, Uz and Hul, and Gether and Mash.
10.24: Also Arpachshad begat Shelah, and Shelah begat Eber.
10.25: Unto Eber also were borne two sonnes: the name of the one was Peleg: for in his dayes was the earth divided: and his brothers name was Joktan.
10.26: Then Joktan begat Almodad and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
10.27: And Hadoram, and Uzal, and Dicklah,
10.28: And Obal, and Abimael, and Sheba,
10.29: And Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab: all these were the sonnes of Joktan.
10.30: And their dwelling was from Mesha, as thou goest unto Sephar a mount of the East.
10.31: These are the sonnes of Shem according to their families, according to their tongues, in their countreis and nations.
10.32: These are the families of the sonnes of Noah, after their generations among their people: and out of these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood.

11.1: Then the whole earth was of one language and one speache.
11.2: And as they went from the East, they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and there they abode.
11.3: And they said one to another, Come, let us make brick, and burn it in the fire. So they had brick for stone, and slime had they in stead of morter.
11.4: Also they said, Goe to, let us build us a citie and a towre, whose top may reach unto the heaven, that we may get us a name, lest we be scattered upon the whole earth.
11.5: But the Lord came down, to see the citie and towre, which the sonnes of men builded.
11.6: And the Lord said, Behold, the people is one, and they all have one language, and this they begin to doe, neither can they now be stopped from whatsoever they have imagined to do.
11.7: Come on, let us goe down, and there confound their language, that every one perceive not anothers speache.
11.8: So ye Lord scattered them from thence upon all the earth, and they left off to build the citie.
11.9: Therefore the name of it was called Babel, because the Lord did there confound the language of all the earth: from thence then did the Lord scatter them upon all the earth.
11.10: These are the generations of Shem: Shem was an hundreth yeere old, and begat Arpachshad two yeere after the flood.
11.11: And Shem lived, after he begat Arpachshad, five hundreth yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
11.12: Also Arpachshad lived five and thirtie yeeres, and begat Shelah.
11.13: And Arpachshad lived, after he begat Shelah, four hundreth and three yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
11.14: And Shelah lived thirtie yeeres, and begat Eber.
11.15: So Shelah lived, after he begat Eber, four hundreth and three yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
11.16: Likewise Eber lived four and thirtie yeres, and begat Peleg.
11.17: So Eber lived, after he begat Peleg, four hundreth and thirtie yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters
11.18: And Peleg lived thirtie yeeres, and begat Reu.
11.19: And Peleg lived, after he begat Reu, two hundreth and nine yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
11.20: Also Reu lived two and thirtie yeeres, and begat Serug.
11.21: So Reu lived, after he begat Serug, two hundreth and seven yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
11.22: Moreover Serug lived thirtie yeeres, and begat Nahor.
11.23: And Serug lived, after he begat Nahor, two hundreth yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
11.24: And Nahor lived nine and twentie yeeres, and begat Terah.
11.25: So Nahor lived, after he begat Terah, an hundreth and nineteen yeeres, and begat sonnes and daughters.
11.26: So Terah lived seuentie yeeres, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
11.27: Now these are the generations of Terah: Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran: and Haran begat Lot.
11.28: Then Haran died before Terah his father in the land of his natiuitie, in Ur of the Caldees.
11.29: So Abram and Nahor took them wives. The name of Abrams wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahors wife Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah, and the father of Iscah.
11.30: But Sarai was barren, and had no child.
11.31: Then Terah took Abram his sonne, and Lot the sonne of Haran, his sonnes sonne, and Sarai his daughter in law, his sonne Abrams wife: and they departed together from Ur of the Caldees, to goe into the land of Canaan, and they came to Haran, and dwelt there.
11.32: So the dayes of Terah were two hundreth and five yeeres, and Terah died in Haran.

12.1: For the Lord had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy countrey, and from thy kindred, and from thy fathers house unto the land that I will shew thee.
12.2: And I will make of thee a great nation, and will bless thee, and make thy name great, and thou shalt be a blessing.
12.3: I will also bless them that bless thee, and curse them that curse thee, and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
12.4: So Abram departed, even as ye Lord spake unto him, and Lot went with him. (And Abram was seuentie and five yeere old, when he departed out of Haran)
12.5: Then Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brothers sonne, and all their substance that they possessed, and the soules that they had gotten in Haran, and they departed, to goe to the land of Canaan: and to the land of Canaan they came.
12.6: So Abram passed through the land unto the place of Shechem, and unto the plain of Moreh (and the Canaanite was then in ye land)
12.7: And the Lord appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land. And there builded he an altar unto the Lord, which appeared unto him.
12.8: Afterward removing thence unto a moutaine Eastward from Beth-el, he pitched his tent having Beth-el on the Westside, and Haai on the East: and there he built an altar unto the Lord, and called on the Name of the Lord.
12.9: Again Abram went forth going and journeying toward the South.
12.10: Then there came a famine in the land: therefore Abram went down into Egypt to soiourne there: for there was a great famine in the land.
12.11: And when he drew neere to enter into Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon:
12.12: Therefore it will come to pass, that when the Egyptians see thee, they will say, She is his wife: so will they kill me, but they will keep thee alive.
12.13: Say, I pray thee, that thou art my sister, that I may fare well for thy sake, and that my life may be preserved by thee.
12.14: Now when Abram was come into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld the woman: for she was very fair.
12.15: And the Princes of Pharaoh saw her, and commended her unto Pharaoh: so the woman was taken into Pharaohs house:
12.16: Who intreated Abram well for her sake, and he had sheep, and beeves, and hee asses, and men servants and maid servants, and she asses, and camelles.
12.17: But the Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues, because of Sarai Abrams wife.
12.18: Then Pharaoh called Abram, and said, Why hast thou done this unto me? Wherefore diddest thou not tell me, that she was thy wife?
12.19: Why saidest thou, She is my sister, that I should take her to be my wife? Now therefore behold thy wife, take her and goe thy way.
12.20: And Pharaoh gave men commandement concerning him: and they conveyed him forth, and his wife, and all that he had.

13.1: Then Abram went up from Egypt, he, and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him toward the South.
13.2: And Abram was very rich in cattell, in silver and in gold.
13.3: And he went on his journey from ye South toward Beth-el, to the place where his tent had been at ye beginning, between Beth-el and Haai,
13.4: Unto the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first: and there Abram called on the Name of the Lord.
13.5: And Lot also, who went with Abram, had sheep, and cattell and tentes,
13.6: So that the land could not bear them, that they might dwell together: for their substance was great, so that they could not dwell together.
13.7: Also there was debate between ye heardmen of Abrams cattell, and the heardmen of Lots cattell. (and the Canaanites and the Perizzites dwelled at that time in the land.)
13.8: Then said Abram unto Lot, Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between thee and me, neither between mine heardmen and thine heardmen: for we be brethren.
13.9: Is not the whole land before thee? depart I pray thee from me: if thou wilt take the left hand, then I will goe to the right: or if thou goe to the right hand, then I will take the left.
13.10: So when Lot lifted up his eyes, he saw that all the plain of Iorden was watered every where: (for before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorah, it was as the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt, as thou goest unto Zoar)
13.11: Then Lot chose unto him all the plain of Iorden, and took his journey from the East: and they departed the one from the other.
13.12: Abram dwelled in the land of Canaan, and Lot abode in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent even to Sodom.
13.13: Now the men of Sodom were wicked and exceeding sinners against the Lord.
13.14: Then the Lord said unto Abram, (after that Lot was departed from him) Lift up thine eyes now, and look from the place where thou art, Northward, and Southward, and Eastward, and Westward:
13.15: For all the land, which thou seest, will I give unto thee and to thy seed for ever,
13.16: And I will make thy seed, as the dust of the earth: so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then shall thy seed be numbred.
13.17: Arise, walk through the land, in ye length thereof, and breadth thereof: for I will give it unto thee.
13.18: Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelled in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and builded there an altar unto ye Lord.

14.1: And in the dayes of Amraphel King of Shinar, Arioch King of Ellasar, Chedor-laomer King of Elam, and Tidal king of the nations:
14.2: These men made war with Bera King of Sodom, and with Birsha King of Gomorah, Shinab King of Admah, and Shemeber King of Zeboiim, and the King of Bela, which is Zoar.
14.3: All these ioyned together in the vale of Siddim, which is the salt Sea.
14.4: Twelve yeere were they subiect to Chedor-laomer, but in the thirteenth yeere they rebelled.
14.5: And in the fourteenth yeere came Chedor-laomer, and the Kings that were with him, and smote the Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim, and the Zuzims in Ham, and the Emims in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
14.6: And the Horites in their mount Seir, unto the plain of Paran, which is by the wilderness.
14.7: And they returned and came to En-mishpat, which is Kadesh, and smote all the countrey of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites that dwelled in Hazezon-tamar.
14.8: Then went out the King of Sodom, and the King of Gomorah, and the King of Admah, and the King of Zeboiim, and the King of Bela, which is Zoar: and they ioyned battell with them in the vale of Siddim:
14.9: To wit, with Chedor-laomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of nations, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar: four Kings against five.
14.10: Now the vale of Siddim was full of slime pits, and the Kings of Sodom and Gomorah fled and fell there: and ye residue fled to the mountain.
14.11: Then they took all the substance of Sodom and Gomorah, and al their vitailes and went their way.
14.12: They took Lot also Abrams brothers sonne and his substance (for he dwelt at Sodom) and departed.
14.13: Then came one that had escaped, and told Abram the Ebrew, which dwelt in the plain of Mamre ye Amorite, brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner, which were confederat with Abram.
14.14: When Abram heard that his brother was taken, he brought forth of them that were borne and brought up in his house, three hundreth and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan.
14.15: Then he, and his servants deuided them selves against them by night, and smote them and pursued them unto Hobah, which is on the left side of Damascus,
14.16: And he recovered all the substance, and also brought again his brother Lot, and his goods, and the women also and the people.
14.17: After that he returned from the slaughter of Chedor-laomer, and of the Kings that were with him, came the King of Sodom foorth to meet him in the valley of Shaveh, which is the Kings dale.
14.18: And Melchi-zedek King of Shalem brought foorth bread and wine: and he was a Priest of the most high God.
14.19: Therefore he blessed him, saying, Blessed art thou, Abram, of God most high possessour of heaven and earth,
14.20: And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thine hand. And Abram gave him tythe of all.
14.21: Then the King of Sodom said to Abram, Give me the persons, and take the goodes to thy self.
14.22: And Abram said to the King of Sodom, I have lift up mine hand unto the Lord the most hie God possessor of heaven and earth,
14.23: That I will not take of all that is thine, so much as a threde or shoolatchet, lest thou shouldest say, I have made Abram rich,
14.24: Save onely that, which the yong men have eaten, and the partes of the men which went with me, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre: let them take their partes.

15.1: After these things, the word of the Lord came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram, I am thy buckler, and thine exceeding great reward.
15.2: And Abram said, O Lord God, what wilt thou give me, seeing I goe childless, and the steward of mine house is this Eliezer of Damascus?
15.3: Again Abram said, Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: wherefore loe, a servant of mine house shalbe mine heir.
15.4: Then behold, the word of the Lord came unto him, saying, This man shall not be thine heir, but one that shall come out of thine own bowels, he shalbe thine heir.
15.5: Moreover he brought him forth and said, Look up now unto heaven, and tell ye starres, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.
15.6: And Abram beleeued the Lord, and he counted that to him for righteousness.
15.7: Again he said unto him, I am the Lord, that brought thee out of Ur of the Caldees, to give thee this land to inherit it.
15.8: And he said, O Lord God, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?
15.9: Then he said unto him, Take me an heifer of three yeeres old, and a she goat of three yeeres old, and a ramme of three yeeres old, a turtle dove also and a pigeon.
15.10: So he took all these unto him, and deuided them into the middes, and laid every piece one against an other: but the birdes deuided he not.
15.11: Then foules fell on the carkases, and Abram drove them away.
15.12: And when the sunne went down, there fell an heauie sleep upon Abram: and loe, a very fearefull darkenes fell upon him.
15.13: Then he said to Abram, Know for a suretie, that thy seed shalbe a stranger in a land, that is not theirs, four hundreth yeeres, and shall serve them: and they shall intreat them evil.
15.14: Notwithstanding the nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.
15.15: But thou shalt goe unto thy fathers in peace, and shalt be buried in a good age.
15.16: And in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the wickednes of the Amorites is not yet full.
15.17: Also when the sunne went down, there was a darkenes: and behold, a smoking fornace, and a firebrand, which went between those pieces.
15.18: In that same day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates.
15.19: The Kenites, and the Kenizites, and the Kadmonites,
15.20: And the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Rephaims,
15.21: The Amorites also, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.

16.1: Now Sarai Abrams wife bare him no children, and she had a maid an Egyptian, Hagar by name.
16.2: And Sarai said unto Abram, Behold now, the Lord hath restrained me from child bearing. I pray thee goe in unto my maid: it may be that I shall receive a child by her. And Abram obeyed the voyce of Sarai.
16.3: Then Sarai Abrams wife took Hagar her maid the Egyptian, after Abram had dwelled ten yeere in the land of Canaan, and gave her to her husband Abram for his wife.
16.4: And he went in unto Hagar, and she conceived. and when she saw that she had conceived, her dame was despised in her eyes.
16.5: Then Sarai said to Abram, Thou doest me wrong. I have given my maid into thy bosom, and she seeth that she hath conceived, and I am despised in her eyes: the Lord judge between me and thee.
16.6: Then Abram said to Sarai, Behold, thy maid is in thine hand: doe with her as it pleaseth thee. Then Sarai dealt roughly with her: wherefore she fled from her.
16.7: But the Angel of the Lord found her beside a fountain of water in the wilderness by the fountain in the way to Shur,
16.8: And he said, Hagar Sarais maid, whence comest thou? and whither wilt thou goe? And she said, I flie from my dame Sarai.
16.9: Then the Angel of the Lord said to her, Return to thy dame, and humble thy self under her hands.
16.10: Again the Angel of the Lord said unto her, I will so greatly increase thy seed, that it shall not be numbred for multitude.
16.11: Also the Angel of the Lord said unto her, See, thou art with child, and shalt bear a sonne, and shalt call his name Ishmael: for the Lord hath heard thy tribulation.
16.12: And he shalbe a wild man: his hand shall be against every man, and every mans hand against him. and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.
16.13: Then she called the name of the Lord, that spake unto her, Thou God lookest on me: for she said, Have I not also here looked after him that seeth me?
16.14: Wherefore the well was called, Beerlahai-roi. lo, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
16.15: And Hagar bare Abram a sonne, and Abram called his sonnes name, which Hagar bare, Ishmael.
16.16: And Abram was four score and six yeere old, when Hagar bare him Ishmael.

17.1: When Abram was ninetie yeere old and nine, the Lord appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am God all sufficient. walk before me, and be thou upright,
17.2: And I will make my covenant between me and thee, and I will multiplie thee exceedingly.
17.3: Then Abram fell on his face, and God talked with him, saying,
17.4: Behold, I make my covenant with thee, and thou shalt be a father of many nations,
17.5: Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shalbe Abraham: for a father of many nations have I made thee.
17.6: Also I will make thee exceeding fruitful, and will make nations of thee: yea, Kings shall proceed of thee.
17.7: Moreover I wil establish my covenant between me and thee, and thy seed after thee in their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be God unto thee and to thy seed after thee.
17.8: And I will give thee and thy seed after thee the land, wherein thou art a stranger, even all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession, and I will be their God.
17.9: Again God said unto Abraham, Thou also shalt keep my covenant, thou, and thy seed after thee in their generations.
17.10: This is my covenant which ye shall keep between me and you, and thy seed after thee, Let every man child among you be circumcised:
17.11: That is, ye shall circumcise the foreskin of your flesh, and it shalbe a sign of the covenant between me and you.
17.12: And every man child of eight dayes old among you, shalbe circumcised in your generations, aswell he that is borne in thine house, as he that is bought with money of any stranger, which is not of thy seed.
17.13: He that is borne in thine house, and he that is bought with thy money, must needes be circumcised: so my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
17.14: But the uncircumcised man child, in whose flesh the foreskin is not circumcised, even that person shall be cut off from his people, because he hath broken my covenant.
17.15: Afterward God said unto Abraham, Sarai thy wife shalt thou not call Sarai, but Sarah shalbe her name.
17.16: And I will bless her, and will also give thee a sonne of her, yea, I will bless her, and she shall be the mother of nations: Kings also of people shall come of her.
17.17: Then Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, Shall a child be borne unto him, that is an hundreth yeere old? and shall Sarah that is ninetie yeere old bear?
17.18: And Abraham said unto God, Oh, that Ishmael might live in thy sight.
17.19: Then God said, Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a sonne in deed, and thou shalt call his name Izhak: and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.
17.20: And as concerning Ishmael, I have heard thee: loe, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiplie him exceedingly: twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make a great nation of him.
17.21: But my covenant will I establish with Izhak, which Sarah shall bear unto thee, the next yeere at this season.
17.22: And he left off talking with him, and God went up from Abraham.
17.23: Then Abraham took Ishmael his sonne and all that were borne in his house, and all that was bought with his money, that is, every man child among the men of Abrahams house, and he circumcised the foreskinne of their flesh in that self same day, as God had comaunded him.
17.24: Abraham also himself was ninetie yeere old and nine, when the foreskinne of his flesh was circumcised.
17.25: And Ishmael his sonne was thirteen yeere old, when the foreskinne of his flesh was circumcised.
17.26: The self same day was Abraham circumcised, and Ishmael his sonne:
17.27: And all the men of his house, both borne in his house, and bought with money of the stranger, were circumcised with him.

18.1: Again the Lord appeared unto him in the plain of Mamre, as he sat in his tent door about the heat of the day.
18.2: And he lift up his eyes, and looked: and lo, three men stood by him, and when he saw them, he ranne to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the ground.
18.3: And he said, Lord, if I have now found fauour in thy sight, goe not, I pray thee, from thy servant.
18.4: Let a litle water, I pray you, be brought, and wash your feet, and rest your selves under the tree.
18.5: And I will bring a morsel of bread, that you may comfort your hearts, afterward ye shall go your wayes: for therefore are ye come to your servant. And they said, Do even as thou hast said.
18.6: Then Abraham made haste into the tent unto Sarah, and said, Make ready at once three measures of fine meal: knead it, and make cakes upon the hearth.
18.7: And Abraham ranne to the beastes, and took a tender and good calf, and gave it to the servant, who hasted to make it ready.
18.8: And he took butter and milk, and the calf, which he had prepared, and set before them, and stood himself by them under the tree, and they did eat.
18.9: Then they said to him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he answered, Behold, she is in the tent.
18.10: And he said, I will certainely come again unto thee according to ye time of life: and loe, Sarah thy wife shall have a sonne. and Sarah heard in the tent door, which was behind him.
18.11: (Now Abraham and Sarah were old and striken in age, and it ceased to be with Sarah after the maner of women)
18.12: Therefore Sarah laughed within her self, saying, After I am waxed old, and my lord also, shall I have lust?
18.13: And ye Lord said unto Abraham, Wherefore did Sarah thus laugh, saying, Shall I certainely bear a child, which am old?
18.14: (Shall any thing be hard to the Lord? at the time appointed will I return unto thee, even according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a sonne.)
18.15: But Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not: for she was afraid. And he said, It is not so: for thou laughedst.
18.16: Afterward the men did rise up from thence and looked toward Sodom: and Abraham went with them to bring them on the way.
18.17: And the Lord said, Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I doe,
18.18: Seeing that Abraham shalbe in deed a great and a mightie nation, and all the nations of the earth shalbe blessed in him?
18.19: For I know him that he will command his sonnes and his houshold after him, that they keep the way of the Lord, to doe righteousness and iudgement, that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that he hath spoken unto him.
18.20: Then the Lord said, Because the crie of Sodom and Gomorah is great, and because their sinne is exceeding grieuous,
18.21: I will goe down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to that crie which is come unto me: and if not, that I may know.
18.22: And the men turned thence and went toward Sodom: but Abraham stood yet before the Lord.
18.23: Then Abraham drew neere, and said, Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked?
18.24: If there be fiftie righteous within the citie, wilt thou destroy and not spare the place for the fiftie righteous that are therein?
18.25: Be it far from thee from doing this thing, to slay the righteous with the wicked: and that the righteous should be even as the wicked, be it far from thee. shall not the Judge of all the world doe right?
18.26: And the Lord answered, If I shall find in Sodom fiftie righteous within the citie, then will I spare all the place for their sakes.
18.27: Then Abraham answered and said, Behold now, I have begun to speak unto my Lord, and I am but dust and ashes.
18.28: If there shall lack five of fiftie righteous, wilt thou destroy all the citie for five? And he said, If I find there five and fourtie, I will not destroy it.
18.29: And he yet spake to him again, and said, What if there shalbe found fourtie there? Then he answered, I will not doe it for fourties sake.
18.30: Again he said, Let not my Lord now be angry, that I speak, What if thirtie be found there? Then he said, I will not doe it, if I find thirtie there.
18.31: Moreover he said, Behold, now I have begonne to speak unto my Lord, What if twentie be found there? And he answered, I will not destroy it for twenties sake.
18.32: Then he said, Let not my Lord be now angrie, and I will speak but this once, What if tenne be found there? And he answered, I will not destroy it for tennes sake.
18.33: And the Lord went his way when he had left communing with Abraham, and Abraham returned unto his place.

19.1: And in the evening there came two Angels to Sodom: and Lot sat at the gate of Sodom, and Lot saw them, and rose up to meet them, and he bowed himself with his face to the ground.
19.2: And he said, See my Lords, I pray you turn in now into your servants house, and tarie all night, and wash your feet, and ye shall rise up early and goe your wayes. Who said, Nay, but we will abide in the street all night.
19.3: Then he preassed upon them earnestly, and they turned in to him, and came to his house, and he made them a feast, and did bake vnleauened bread, and they did eat.
19.4: But before they went to bed, the men of the citie, even the men of Sodom compassed the house round about from the yong even to the old, all the people from all quarters.
19.5: Who crying unto Lot said to him, Where are the men, which came to thee this night? bring them out unto us that we may know them.
19.6: Then Lot went out at the door unto them, and shut the door after him,
19.7: And said, I pray you, my brethren, do not so wickedly.
19.8: Behold now, I have two daughters, which have not knowen man: them will I bring out now unto you, and doe to them as seemeth you good: onely unto these men doe nothing: for therefore are they come under the shadow of my roof.
19.9: Then they said, Away hence, and they said, He is come alone as a stranger, and shall he judge and rule? we will now deal worse with thee then with them. So they preassed sore upon Lot himself, and came to break the door.
19.10: But the men put forth their hand and pulled Lot into the house to them and shut to ye door.
19.11: Then they smote the men that were at the door of the house with blindnes both small and great, so that they were wearie in seeking the door.
19.12: Then the men said unto Lot, Whom hast thou yet here? either sonne in law, or thy sonnes, or thy daughters, or whatsoever thou hast in the citie, bring it out of this place.
19.13: For we will destroy this place, because the cry of them is great before the Lord, and the Lord hath sent us to destroy it.
19.14: Then Lot went out and spake unto his sonnes in law, which maried his daughters, and said, Arise, get you out of this place: for the Lord will destroy the citie: but he seemed to his sonnes in law as though he had mocked.
19.15: And when the morning arose, the Angels hasted Lot, saying, Arise, take thy wife and thy two daughters which are here, lest thou be destroyed in the punishment of the citie.
19.16: And as he prolonged the time, the men caught both him and his wife, and his two daughters by the hands (the Lord being merciful unto him) and they brought him foorth, and set him without the citie.
19.17: And when they had brought them out, the Angel said, Escape for thy life: look not behind thee, neither tarie thou in all the plain: escape into ye mountain, least thou be destroyed.
19.18: And Lot said unto them, Not so, I pray thee, my Lord.
19.19: Behold now, thy servant hath found grace in thy sight, and thou hast magnified thy mercie, which thou hast shewed unto me in saving my life: and I cannot escape in the mountain, least some evil take me, and I die.
19.20: See now this citie hereby to flee unto, which is a litle one: Oh let me escape thither: is it not a litle one, and my soul shall live?
19.21: Then he said unto him, Behold, I have received thy request also concerning this thing, that I will not overthrow this citie, for the which thou hast spoken.
19.22: Haste thee, save thee there: for I can doe nothing till thou be come thither. Therefore the name of the citie was called Zoar.
19.23: The sunne did rise upon the earth, when Lot entred into Zoar.
19.24: Then the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorah brimstone, and fire from the Lord out of heaven,
19.25: And overthrew those cities and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities; and that that grew upon the earth.
19.26: Now his wife behind him looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
19.27: And Abraham rising up earely in ye morning went to the place, where he had stand before the Lord,
19.28: And looking toward Sodom and Gomorah and toward all the land of the plain, behold, he saw the smoke of the land mounting up as the smoke of a fornace.
19.29: But yet when God destroyed the cities of the plain, God thought upon Abraham, and sent Lot out from the middes of the destruction, when he overthrew the cities, wherein Lot dwelled.
19.30: Then Lot went up from Zoar, and dwelt in the mountain with his two daughters: for he feared to tarie in Zoar, but dwelt in a cave, he, and his two daughters.
19.31: And the elder said unto the yonger, Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth, to come in unto us after the maner of all ye earth.
19.32: Come, wee will make our father drink wine, and lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.
19.33: So they made their father drink wine that night, and the elder went and lay with her father: but he perceived not, neither whe she lay down, neither when she rose up.
19.34: And on the morowe the elder said to the yonger, Behold, yester night lay I with my father: let us make him drink wine this night also, and goe thou and lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.
19.35: So they made their father drink wine that night also, and the yonger arose, and lay with him, but he perceived not, when she lay down, neither when she rose up.
19.36: Thus were both the daughters of Lot with child by their father.
19.37: And the elder bare a sonne, and she called his name Moab: the same is the father of the Moabites unto this day.
19.38: And the yonger bare a sonne also, and she called his name Ben-ammi: the same is the father of the Ammonites unto this day.

20.1: Afterward Abraham departed thence toward the South countrey and dwelled between Cadesh and Shur, and soiourned in Gerar.
20.2: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, She is my sister. Then Abimelech King of Gerar sent and took Sarah.
20.3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and said to him, Behold, thou art but dead, because of the woman, which thou hast taken: for she is a mans wife.
20.4: (Notwithstanding Abimelech had not yet come neere her) And he said, Lord, wilt thou slay even the righteous nation?
20.5: Said not he unto me, She is my sister? yea, and she her self said, He is my brother: with an upright mind, and innocent handes have I done this.
20.6: And God said unto him by a dream, I know that thou diddest this even with an upright mind, and I kept thee also that thou shouldest not sinne against me: therefore suffered I thee not to touch her.
20.7: Now then deliver the man his wife again: for he is a Prophet, and he shall pray for thee that thou mayest live: but if thou deliver her not again, be sure that thou shalt die the death, thou, and all that thou hast.
20.8: Then Abimelech rising up early in ye morning, called all his servants, and told all these things unto them, and the men were sore afraid.
20.9: Afterward Abimelech called Abraham, and said unto him, What hast thou done unto us? and what have I offeded thee, that thou hast brought on me and on my kingdom this great sinne? thou hast done things unto me that ought not to be done.
20.10: So Abimelech said unto Abraham, What sawest thou that thou hast done this thing?
20.11: Then Abraham answered, Because I thought thus, Surely the fear of God is not in this place, and they will slay me for my wives sake.
20.12: Yet in very deed she is my sister: for she is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother, and she is my wife.
20.13: Now when God caused me to wander out of my fathers house, I said then to her, This is thy kindnes that thou shalt shew unto me in all places where we come, Say thou of me, He is my brother.
20.14: Then took Abimelech sheep and beeves, and men servants, and women servants, and gave them unto Abraham, and restored him Sarah his wife.
20.15: And Abimelech said, Behold, my land is before thee: dwell where it pleaseth thee.
20.16: Likewise to Sarah he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver: behold, he is the vail of thine eyes to all that are with thee, and to all others: and she was thus reproved.
20.17: Then Abraham prayed unto God, and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his women servants: and they bare children.
20.18: For the Lord had shut up every womb of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah Abrahams wife.

21.1: Now the Lord visited Sarah, as he had said, and did unto her according as he had promised.
21.2: For Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a sonne in his old age, at the same season that God told him.
21.3: And Abraham called his sonnes name that was borne unto him, which Sarah bare him, Izhak.
21.4: Then Abraham circumcised Izhak his sonne, when he was eight dayes old, as God had commanded him.
21.5: So Abraham was an hundreth yeere old, when his sonne Izhak was borne unto him.
21.6: Then Sarah said, God hath made me to reioyce: all that hear will reioyce with me.
21.7: Again she said, Who would have said to Abraham, that Sarah should have given children suck? for I have borne him a sonne in his old age.
21.8: Then the child grew and was weaned: and Abraham made a great feast the same day that Izhak was weaned.
21.9: And Sarah saw the sonne of Hagar the Egyptian (which she had borne unto Abraham) mocking.
21.10: Wherefore she said unto Abraham, Cast out this bond woman and her sonne: for ye sonne of this bond woman shall not be heir with my sonne Izhak.
21.11: And this thing was very grieuous in Abrahams sight, because of his sonne.
21.12: But God said unto Abraham, Let it not be grieuous in thy sight for the child, and for thy bond woman: in all that Sarah shall say unto thee, hear her voyce: for in Izhak shall thy seed be called.
21.13: As for the sonne of the bond woman, I will make him a nation also, because he is thy seed.
21.14: So Abraham arose up early in ye morning, and took bread, and a bottell of water, and gave it unto Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, and the child also, and sent her away: who departing wandred in the wilderness of Beer-sheba.
21.15: And when the water of the bottell was spent, she cast the child under a certain tree.
21.16: Then she went and sat her over against him a far off about a bow shoot: for she said, I will not see the death of the child. and she sat down over against him, and lift up her voyce and wept.
21.17: Then God heard the voyce of ye child, and the Angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, and said unto her, What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not, for God hath heard the voyce of the child where he is.
21.18: Arise, take up the child, and hold him in thine hand: for I will make of him a great people.
21.19: And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. so she went and filled the bottell with water, and gave the boy drink.
21.20: So God was with the child, and he grew and dwelt in the wilderness, and was an archer.
21.21: And he dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took him a wife out of the land of Egypt.
21.22: And at that same time Abimelech and Phichol his chief captain spake unto Abraham, saying, God is with thee in all that thou doest.
21.23: Now therefore swear unto me here by God, that thou wilt not hurt me, nor my children, nor my childrens children: thou shalt deal with me, and with the countrey, where thou hast been a stranger, according unto the kindness that I have shewed thee.
21.24: Then Abraham said, I will swear.
21.25: And Abraham rebuked Abimelech for a well of water, which Abimelechs servants had violently taken away.
21.26: And Abimelech said, I know not who hath done this thing: also thou toldest me not, neither heard I of it but this day.
21.27: Then Abraham took sheep and beeves, and gave them unto Abimelech: and they two made a covenant.
21.28: And Abraham set seven lambes of the flock by themselves.
21.29: Then Abimelech said unto Abraham, What mean these seven lambes, which thou hast set by themselves?
21.30: And he answered, Because thou shalt receive of mine hand these seven lambes, that it may be a witnes unto me, that I have digged this well.
21.31: Wherefore the place is called Beer-sheba, because there they both sware.
21.32: Thus made they a covenant at Beer-sheba: afterward Abimelech and Phichol his chief captain rose up, and turned again unto the land of the Philistims.
21.33: And Abraham planted a grove in Beer-sheba, and called there on the Name of ye Lord, the everlasting God.
21.34: And Abraham was a stranger in the Philistims land a long season.

22.1: And after these things God did prove Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham. Who answered, Here am I.
22.2: And he said, Take now thine onely sonne Izhak whom thou lovest, and get thee unto the land of Moriah, and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountaines, which I will shew thee.
22.3: Then Abraham rose up early in the morning, and sadled his ass, and took two of his servants with him, and Izhak his sonne, and cloue wood for the burnt offering, and rose up and went to the place, which God had told him.
22.4: Then the third day Abraham lift up his eyes, and saw the place afarre off,
22.5: And said unto his servants, Abide you here with the ass: for I and the child will go yonder and worship, and come again unto you.
22.6: Then Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering, and layed it upon Izhak his sonne, and he took the fire in his hand, and the knife: and they went both together.
22.7: Then spake Izhak unto Abraham his father, and said, My father. And he answered, Here am I, my sonne. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for ye burnt offring?
22.8: Then Abraham answered, My sonne, God will provide him a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both together.
22.9: And when they came to the place which God had shewed him, Abraham builded an altar there, and couched ye wood, and bound Izhak his sonne and laid him on the altar upon the wood.
22.10: And Abraham stretching forth his hand, took the knife to kill his sonne.
22.11: But the Angel of the Lord called unto him from heaven, saying, Abraham, Abraham. And he answered, Here am I.
22.12: Then he said, Lay not thine hand upon the child, neither doe any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing for my sake thou hast not spared thine onely sonne.
22.13: And Abraham lifting up his eyes, looked: and behold, there was a ramme behind him caught by the hornes in a bush. then Abraham went and took the ramme, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his sonne.
22.14: And Abraham called the name of that place, Jehovah-ijreh. as it is said this day, In the mount will the Lord be seen.
22.15: And the Angel of the Lord cryed unto Abraham from heaven the second time,
22.16: And said, By my self have I sworn (saith ye Lord) because thou hast done this thing, and hast not spared thine onely sonne,
22.17: Therefore will I surely bless thee, and will greatly multiplie thy seed, as the starres of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore, and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.
22.18: And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, because thou hast obeyed my voyce.
22.19: Then turned Abraham again unto his servants, and they rose up and went together to Beer-sheba: and Abraham dwelt at Beer-sheba.
22.20: And after these things one told Abraham, saying, Behold Milcah, she hath also borne children unto thy brother Nahor:
22.21: To wit, Uz his eldest sonne, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
22.22: And Chesed and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
22.23: And Bethuel begat Rebekah: these eight did Milcah bear to Nahor Abrahams brother.
22.24: And his concubine called Reumah, she bare also Tebah, and Gahan, and Thahash and Maachah.

23.1: When Sarah was an hundreth twentie and seven yeere old (so long lived she).
23.2: Then Sarah dyed in Kiriath-arba: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan. and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
23.3: Then Abraham rose up from the sight of his corps, and talked with the Hittites, saying,
23.4: I am a stranger, and a forreiner among you, give me a possession of burial with you, that I may burie my dead out of my sight.
23.5: Then the Hittites answered Abraham, saying unto him,
23.6: Hear us, my lord: thou art a prince of God among us: in the chiefest of our sepulchres bury thy dead: none of us shall forbid thee his sepulchre, but thou mayest bury thy dead therein.
23.7: Then Abraham stood up, and bowed him self before the people of the land of the Hittites.
23.8: And he communed with them, saying, If it be your mind, that I shall bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and intreat for me to Ephron the sonne of Zohar,
23.9: That he would give me ye cave of Machpelah, which he hath in the end of his field: that he would give it me for as much money as it is worth, for a possession to bury in among you.
23.10: (For Ephron dwelt among the Hittites) Then Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the audience of all the Hittites that went in at the gates of his citie, saying,
23.11: No, my Lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave, that therein is, I give it thee: even in the presence of the sonnes of my people give I it thee, to bury thy dead.
23.12: Then Abraham bowed himself before the people of the land,
23.13: And spake unto Ephron in the audience of the people of the countrey, saying, Seeing thou wilt give it, I pray thee, hear me, I will give the price of the field: receive it of me, and I will bury my dead there.
23.14: Ephron then answered Abraham, saying unto him,
23.15: My lord, hearken unto me: ye land is worth four hundreth shekels of silver: what is that between me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.
23.16: So Abraham hearkened unto Ephron, and Abraham weyed to Ephron the silver, which he had named, in the audience of the Hittites, even four hundreth silver shekels of currant money among marchants.
23.17: So the field of Ephron which was in Machpelah, and over against Mamre, even the field and the cave that was therein, and all the trees that were in the field, which were in all the borders round about, was made sure
23.18: Unto Abraham for a possession, in ye sight of the Hittites, even of all that went in at the gates of his citie.
23.19: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah over against Mamre: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan.
23.20: Thus the field and the cave, that is therein, was made sure unto Abraham for a possession of burial by the Hittites.

24.1: Now Abraham was old, and striken in yeeres, and the Lord had blessed Abraham in all things.
24.2: Therefore Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house, which had the rule over all that he had, Put now thine hand under my thigh,
24.3: And I will make thee swear by ye Lord God of the heaven, and God of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my sonne of the daughters of the Canaanites among who I dwel.
24.4: But thou shalt go unto my countrey, and to my kinred, and take a wife unto my son Izhak.
24.5: And the servant said to him, What if the woman will not come with me to this land? shall I bring thy sonne again unto the land from whence thou camest?
24.6: To whom Abraham answered, Beware that thou bring not my sonne thither again.
24.7: The Lord God of heaven, who took me from my fathers house, and from the land where I was borne, and that spake unto me, and that sware unto me, saying, Unto thy seed wil I give this land, he shall send his Angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife unto my sonne from thence.
24.8: Neuertheles if the woman wil not follow thee, then shalt thou bee discharged of this mine othe: onely bring not my sonne thither again.
24.9: Then the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sware to him for this matter.
24.10: So the servant took ten camels of the camels of his master, and departed: (for he had all his masters goods in his hand:) and so he arose, and went to Aram Naharaim, unto the citie of Nahor.
24.11: And he made his camels to lye down without the citie by a well of water, at eventide about the time that the women come out to draw water.
24.12: And he said, O Lord God of my master Abraham, I beseech thee, send me good speed this day, and shew mercy unto my master Abraham.
24.13: Lo, I stand by the well of water, whiles the mens daughters of this citie come out to draw water.
24.14: Graunt therefore that ye maid, to whom I say, Bow down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink: if she say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: may be she that thou hast ordeined for thy servant Izhak: and thereby shall I know that thou hast shewed mercy on my master.
24.15: And now yer he had left speaking, behold, Rebekah came out, the daughter of Bethuel, sonne of Milcah the wife of Nahor Abrahams brother, and her pitcher upon her shoulder.
24.16: (And the maid was very fair to look upon, a virgin and vnknowen of man) and she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher, and came up.
24.17: Then the servant ranne to meet her, and said, Let me drink, I pray thee, a litle water of thy pitcher.
24.18: And she said, Drink sir: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand and gave him drink.
