24.19: And when she had given him drink, she said, I will draw water for thy camels also until they have drunken inough.
24.20: And she powred out her pitcher into the trough speedily; and ranne again unto the well to draw water, and she drew for all his camels.
24.21: So the man wondred at her, and held his peace, to know whether the Lord had made his journey prosperous or not.
24.22: And when the camels had left drinking, the man took a golden abillement of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands, of ten shekels weight of gold:
24.23: And he said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee, Is there roume in thy fathers house for us to lodge in?
24.24: Then she said to him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the sonne of Milcah whom she bare unto Nahor.
24.25: Moreover she said unto him, We have litter also and provender ynough, and roume to lodge in.
24.26: And the man bowed himself and worshipped the Lord,
24.27: And said, Blessed be the Lord God of my master Abraham, which hath not withdrawen his mercie and his trueth from my master: for when I was in the way, the Lord brought me to my masters brethrens house.
24.28: And the maid ranne and told them of her mothers house according to these wordes.
24.29: Now Rebekah had a brother called Laban, and Laban ranne unto the man to the well.
24.30: For when he had seen the earings and the bracelets in his sisters hands, and when he heard the wordes of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus said the man unto me, then he went to the man, and loe, he stood by the camels at the well.
24.31: And he said, Come in thou blessed of the Lord: wherefore standest thou without, seeing I have prepared the house, and roume for ye camels?
24.32: Then the man came into the house, and he vnsadled the camels, and brought litter and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the mens feet that were with him.
24.33: Afterward the meat was set before him: but he said, I will not eat, until I have said my message: And he said, Speak on.
24.34: Then he said, I am Abrahams servant,
24.35: And the Lord hath blessed my master wonderfully, that he is become great: for he hath given him sheep, and beeves, and silver, and gold, and men servants, and maid servants, and camels, and asses.
24.36: And Sarah my masters wife hath borne a sonne to my master, when she was old, and unto him hath he given all that he hath.
24.37: Now my master made me swear, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife to my sonne of the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell:
24.38: But thou shalt go unto my fathers house and to my kinred, and take a wife unto my sonne.
24.39: Then I said unto my master, What if the woman will not follow me?
24.40: Who answered me, The Lord, before who I walk, will send his Angel with thee, and prosper thy journey, and thou shalt take a wife for my sonne of my kinred and my fathers house.
24.41: Then shalt thou be discharged of mine othe, when thou comest to my kinred: and if they give thee not one, thou shalt be free from mine othe.
24.42: So I came this day to the well, and said, O Lord, the God of my master Abraham, if thou now prosper my journey which I goe,
24.43: Behold, I stand by the well of water: when a virgin cometh forth to draw water, and I say to her, Give me, I pray thee, a litle water of thy pitcher to drink,
24.44: And she say to me, Drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels, let her be ye wife, which the Lord hath prepared for my masters sonne.
24.45: And before I had made an end of speaking in mine heart, behold, Rebekah came foorth, and her pitcher on her shoulder, and she went down unto the well, and drew water. Then I said unto her, Give me drink, I pray thee.
24.46: And she made haste, and took down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also. So I drank, and she gave the camels drink also.
24.47: Then I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? And she answered, The daughter of Bethuel Nahors sonne, whom Milcah bare unto him. Then I put the abillement upon her face, and the bracelets upon her hands:
24.48: And I bowed down and worshipped the Lord, and blessed the Lord God of my master Abraham, which had brought me the right way to take my masters brothers daughter unto his son.
24.49: Now therefore, if ye will deal mercifully and truely with my master, tell me: and if not, tell me that I may turn me to the right hand or to the left.
24.50: Then answered Laban and Bethuel, and said, This thing is proceeded of the Lord: we cannot therefore say unto thee, neither evil nor good.
24.51: Behold, Rebehak is before thee, take her and goe, that she may be thy masters sonnes wife, even as the Lord hath said.
24.52: And when Abrahams servant heard their wordes, he bowed himself toward the earth unto the Lord.
24.53: Then the servant took foorth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave to Rebekah: also unto her brother and to her mother he gave gifts.
24.54: Afterward they did eat and drink, both he, and the men that were with him, and taried all night. and when they rose up in the morning, he said, Let me depart unto my master.
24.55: Then her brother and her mother answered, Let the maid abide with us, at the least ten dayes: then shall she goe.
24.56: But he said unto them, Hinder you me not, seeing the Lord hath prospered my journey: send me away, that I may goe to my master.
24.57: Then they said, We will call the maid, and ask her consent.
24.58: And they called Rebekah, and said unto her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she answered, I will go.
24.59: So they let Rebekah their sister goe, and her nourse, with Abrahams servant and his men.
24.60: And they blessed Rebekah, and sayde unto her, Thou art our sister, grow into thousand thousands, and thy seed possess the gate of his enemies.
24.61: Then Rebekah arose, and her maydes, and rode upon the camels, and followed the man. and the servant took Rebekah, and departed.
24.62: Now Izhak came from the way of Beer-lahai-roi, (for he dwelt in the South countrey)
24.63: And Izhak went out. to pray in the field toward the evening: who lift up his eyes and looked, and behold, the camels came.
24.64: Also Rebekah lift up her eyes, and when she saw Izhak, she lighted down from the camel.
24.65: (For she had sayde to the servant, Who is yonder man, that cometh in the field to meet us? and the servant had said, It is my master) So she took a vail, and covered her.
24.66: And the servant told Izhak all things, that he had done.
24.67: Afterward Izhak brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, and he took Rebekah, and she was his wife, and he loved her: So Izhak was comforted after his mothers death.

25.1: Now Abraham had taken him another wife called Keturah,
25.2: Which bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
25.3: And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan: And the sonnes of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim.
25.4: Also the sonnes of Midian were Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah all these were the sonnes of Keturah.
25.5: And Abraham gave all his goods to Izhak,
25.6: But unto the sonnes of the concubines, which Abraham had, Abraham gave giftes, and sent them away from Izhak his sonne (while he yet lived) Eastward to the East countrey.
25.7: And this is the age of Abrahams life, which he lived, an hundreth seuentie and five yeere.
25.8: Then Abraham yeelded the spirit, and died in a good age, an old man, and of great yeeres, and was gathered to his people.
25.9: And his sonnes, Izhak and Ishmael buryed him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron sonne of Zohar the Hittite, before Mamre.
25.10: Which field Abraham bought of the Hittites, where Abraham was buryed with Sarah his wife.
25.11: And after the death of Abraham God blessed Izhak his sonne, and Izhak dwelt by Beer-lahai-roi.
25.12: Now these are the generations of Ishmael Abrahams sonne, whom Hagar the Egyptian Sarahs handmayde bare unto Abraham.
25.13: And these are the names of the sonnes of Ishmael, name by name, according to their kinreds; the eldest sonne of Ishmael was Nebaioth, then Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
25.14: And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
25.15: Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
25.16: These are the sonnes of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their townes and by their castles: to wit, twelve princes of their nations.
25.17: (And these are the yeeres of the life of Ishmael, an hundreth thirtie and seven yeere, and he yeelded the spirit, and dyed, and was gathered unto his people)
25.18: And they dwelt from Havilah unto Shur, that is towardes Egypt, as thou goest to Asshur. Ishmael dwelt in the presence of all his brethren.
25.19: Likewise these are the generations of Izhak Abrahams sonne Abraham begat Izhak,
25.20: And Izhak was fourtie yeere old, when he took Rebekah to wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramite of Padan Aram, and sister to Laban the Aramite.
25.21: And Izhak prayed vuto the Lord for his wife, because she was barren: and the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived,
25.22: But the children strove together within her: therefore she sayde, Seeing it is so, why am I thus? wherefore she went to ask the Lord.
25.23: And the Lord sayd to her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two maner of people shalbe divided out of thy bowels, and the one people shall be mightier then the other, and the elder shall serve the yonger.
25.24: Therefore when her time of deliverance was fulfilled, behold, twinnes were in her womb.
25.25: So he that came out first was red, and he was all over as a rough garment, and they called his name Esau.
25.26: And afterward came his brother out, and his hand held Esau by the heel: therefore his name was called Iaakob. Now Izhak was threescore yeere old when Rebekah bare them.
25.27: And the boyes grew, and Esau was a cunning hunter, and lived in the fields: but Iaakob was a plain man, and dwelt in tentes.
25.28: And Izhak loved Esau, for venison was his meat, but Rebekah loved Iaakob.
25.29: Now Iaakob sod pottage, and Esau came from the field and was wearie.
25.30: Then Esau sayd to Iaakob, Let me eat, I pray thee, of that pottage so red, for I am wearie. Therefore was his name called Edom.
25.31: And Iaakob sayd, Sell me even now thy birthright.
25.32: And Esau sayd, Lo, I am almost dead, what is then this birthright to me?
25.33: Iaakob then said, Swear to me even now. And he sware to him, and sold his birthright unto Iaakob.
25.34: Then Iaakob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles: and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: So Esau contemned his birthright.

26.1: And there was a famine in the land besides the first famine that was in the dayes of Abraham. Wherefore Izhak went to Abimelech King of the Philistims unto Gerar.
26.2: For the Lord appeared unto him, and sayde, Goe not down into Egypt, but abide in the land which I shall shew unto thee.
26.3: Dwell in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee: for to thee, and to thy seed I will give all these countreys: and I will perform the othe which I sware unto Abraham thy father.
26.4: Also I wil cause thy seed to multiply as the starres of heaven, and will give unto thy seed all these countreys: and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed,
26.5: Because that Abraham obeyed my voyce and kept mine ordinance, my commandements, my statutes, and my Lawes.
26.7: And the men of the place asked him of his wife, and he sayd, She is my sister: for he feared to say, She is my wife, least, sayde he, the men of the place should kill me, because of Rebekah: for she was beautiful to the eye.
26.8: So after hee had been there long time, Abimelech King of the Philistims looked out at a window, and loe, he saw Izhak sporting with Rebekah his wife.
26.9: Then Abimelech called Izhak, and sayde, Loe, she is of a suertie thy wife, and why saydest thou, She is my sister? To whom Izhak answered, Because I thought this, It may be that I shall dye for her.
26.10: Then Abimelech said, Why hast thou done this unto us? one of the people had almost lien by thy wife, so shouldest thou have brought sinne upon us.
26.11: Then Abimelech charged all his people, saying, He that toucheth this man, or his wife, shall die the death.
26.12: Afterward Izhak sowed in that land, and found in the same yeere an hundreth fold by estimation: and so the Lord blessed him.
26.13: And the man waxed mightie, and stil increased, till he was exceeding great,
26.14: For he had flockes of sheep, and heards of cattell, and a mightie housholde: therefore the Philistims had envy at him.
26.15: In so much that the Philistims stopped and filled up with earth all the welles, which his fathers seruantes digged in his father Abrahams time.
26.16: Then Abimelech sayde unto Izhak, Get thee from us, for thou art mightier then wee a great deal.
26.17: Therefore Izhak departed thence and pitched his tent in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.
26.18: And Izhak returning, digged the welles of water, which they had digged in the dayes of Abraham his father: for the Philistims had stopped them after the death of Abraham, and hee gave them the same names, which his father gave them.
26.19: Izhaks seruantes then digged in the valley, and found there a well of living water.
26.20: But the herdmen of Gerar did strive with Izhaks herdmen, saying, The water is ours: therefore called he the name of the well Esek, because they were at strife with him.
26.21: Afterward they digged another well, and strove for that also, and he called the name of it Sitnah.
26.22: Then he removed thence, and digged an other well, for the which they strove not: therefore called hee the name of it Rehoboth, and sayde, Because the Lord hath now made us room, we shall increase upon the earth.
26.23: So he went up thence to Beer-sheba.
26.24: And the Lord appeared unto him the same night, and sayde, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am with thee, and wil bless thee, and will multiplie thy seed for my servant Abrahams sake.
26.25: Then he built an altar there, and called upon the Name of the Lord, and there spred his tent: where also Izhaks seruauntes digged a well.
26.26: Then came Abimelech to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath one of his friendes, and Phichol the captain of his armie.
26.27: To whom Izhak sayd, Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate mee and have put mee away from you?
26.28: Who answered, Wee saw certainely that the Lord was with thee, and wee thought thus, Let there be now an othe between us, even between us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee.
26.29: If thou shalt do us no hurt, as we have not touched thee, and as we have done unto thee nothing but good, and sent thee away in peace: thou now, the blessed of the Lord, doe this.
26.30: Then hee made them a feast, and they dyd eat and drink.
26.31: And they rose up betimes in the morning, and sware one to another: then Izhak let them go, and they departed from him in peace.
26.32: And that same day Izhaks seruantes came and told him of a well, which they had digged, and said unto him, We have found water.
26.33: So hee called it Shibah: therefore the name of the citie is called Beer-sheba unto this day.
26.34: Now when Esau was fourtie yeere old, he took to wife Judith, the daughter of Beeri an Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon an Hittite also.
26.35: And they were a grief of mind to Izhak and to Rebekah.

27.1: And when Izhak was old, and his eyes were dimme (so that he could not see) he called Esau his eldest sonne, and sayde unto him, My sonne. And he answered him, I am here.
27.2: Then he sayd, Behold, I am now old, and know not the day of my death:
27.3: Wherefore now, I pray thee take thine instruments, thy quiuer and thy bow, and get thee to the field, that thou mayest take mee some venison.
27.4: Then make mee sauourie meat, such as I love, and bring it me that I may eat, and that my soul may bless thee, before I die.
27.5: (Now Rebekah heard, when Izhak spake to Esau his sonne) and Esau went into the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.
27.6: Then Rebekah spake unto Iaakob her sonne, saying, Behold, I have heard thy father talking with Esau thy brother, saying,
27.7: Bring mee vension, and make mee sauourie meat, that I may eat and bless thee before the Lord, afore my death.
27.8: Now therefore, my sonne, hear my voyce in that which I command thee.
27.9: Get thee now to the flock, and bring me thence two good kids of the goates, that I may make pleasant meat of them for thy father, such as he loveth.
27.10: Then shalt thou bring it to thy father, and he shall eat, to the intent that he may bless thee before his death.
27.11: But Iaakob sayde to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is rough, and I am smooth.
27.12: My father may possibly feel me, and I shall seem to him to be a mocker: so shall I bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.
27.13: But his mother sayd unto him, upon me be thy curse, my sonne: onely hear my voyce, and go and bring me them.
27.14: So he went and set them, and brought them to his mother: and his mother made pleasant meat, such as his father loved.
27.15: And Rebekah took fair clothes of her elder sonne Esau, which were in her house, and clothed Iaakob her yonger sonne:
27.16: And she covered his hands and the smooth of his neck with the skinnes of the kiddes of the goates.
27.17: Afterward she put the pleasant meat and bread, which she had prepared, in the hand of her sonne Iaakob.
27.18: And when he came to his father, he sayd, My father. Who answered, I am here: who art thou, my sonne?
27.19: And Iaakob sayde to his father, I am Esau thy first borne, I have done as thou badest me, arise, I pray thee: sit up and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.
27.20: Then Izhak said unto his sonne, How hast thou found it so quickly my sonne? Who sayde, Because the Lord thy God brought it to mine hand.
27.21: Again sayde Izhak unto Iaakob, Come neere now, that I may feel thee, my sonne, whether thou be that my sonne Esau or not.
27.22: Then Iaakob came neere to Izhak his father, and he felt him and sayd, The voyce is Iaakobs voyce, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
27.23: (For he knew him not, because his hands were rough as his brother Esaus hands: wherefore he blessed him)
27.24: Again he sayd, Art thou that my sonne Esau? Who answered, Yea.
27.25: Then said he, Bring it me hither, and I will eat of my sonnes venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it to him, and he ate: also he brought him wine, and he drank.
27.26: Afterward his father Izhak sayd unto him, Come neere now, and kiss me, my sonne.
27.27: And hee came neere and kissed him. Then he smelled the sauour of his garmentes, and blessed him, and sayde, Behold, the smell of my sonne is as the smell of a field, which the Lord hath blessed.
27.28: God give thee therefore of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plentie of wheat and wine.
27.29: Let people bee thy seruantes, and nations bow unto thee: be Lord over thy brethren, and let thy mothers children honour thee. cursed be he that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.
27.30: And when Izhak had made an end of blessing Iaakob, and Iaakob was scarce gone out from the presence of Izhak his father, then came Esau his brother from his hunting,
27.31: And hee also prepared sauourie meat and brought it to his father, and sayd unto his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his sonnes venison, that thy soul may bless me.
27.32: But his father Izhak sayde unto him, Who art thou? And he answered, I am thy sonne, even thy first borne Esau.
27.33: Then Izhak was stricken with a marueilous great fear, and sayde, Who and where is hee that hunted venison, and brought it mee, and I have eat of all before thou camest? and I have blessed him, therefore he shalbe blessed.
27.34: When Esau heard the wordes of his father, he cryed out with a great cry and bitter, out of measure, and sayde unto his father, Bless me, even me also, my father.
27.35: Who answered, Thy brother came with subtiltie, and hath taken away thy blessing.
27.36: Then he sayde, Was hee not justly called Iaakob? for hee hath deceived mee these two times: he took my birthright, and loe, now hath he taken my blessing. Also he sayd, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?
27.37: Then Izhak answered, and sayd unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethre have I made his servants: also with wheat and wine have I furnished him, and unto thee now what shall I doe, my sonne?
27.38: Then Esau sayde unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing my father? bless mee, even me also, my father: and Esau lifted up his voyce, and wept.
27.39: Then Izhak his father answered, and sayde unto him, Behold, the fatness of the earth shall be thy dwelling place, and thou shalt have of the dew of heaven from above.
27.40: And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt be thy brothers servant. But it shall come to pass, when thou shalt get the masterie, that thou shalt break his yoke from thy neck.
27.41: Therefore Esau hated Iaakob, because of the blessing, wherewith his father blessed him. And Esau thought in his mind, The dayes of mourning for my father will come shortly, then I will slay may brother Iaakob.
27.42: And it was told to Rebekah of the wordes of Esau her elder sonne, and she sent and called Iaakob her yonger sonne, and sayd unto him, Behold, thy brother Esau is comforted against thee, meaning to kill thee:
27.43: Now therefore my sonne, hear my voyce, arise, and flee thou to Haran to my brother Laban,
27.44: And tarie with him a while until thy brothers fierceness be swaged,
27.45: And till thy brothers wrath turn away from thee, and hee forget the thinges, which thou hast done to him: then will I send and take thee from thence: why should I bee deprived of you both in one day?
27.46: Also Rebekah said to Izhak, I am weary of my life, for the daughters of Heth. If Iaakob take a wife of the daughters of Heth like these of the daughters of the land, what availeth it me to live?

28.1: Then Izhak called Iaakob and blessed him, and charged him, and sayde unto him, Take not a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
28.2: Arise, get thee to Padan Aram to the house of Bethuel thy mothers father, and thence take thee a wife of the daughters of Laban thy mothers brother.
28.3: And God all sufficient bless thee, and make thee to encrease, and multiplie thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people,
28.4: And give thee the blessing of Abraham, even to thee and to thy seed with thee, that thou mayest inherit the land (wherein thou art a stranger,) which God gave unto Abraham.
28.5: Thus Izhak sent forth Iaakob, and he went to Padan Aram unto Laban sonne of Bethuel the Aramite, brother to Rebekah, Iaakobs and Esaus mother.
28.6: When Esau saw that Izhak had blessed Iaakob, and sent him to Padan Aram, to set him a wife thence, and given him a charge when he blessed him, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan,
28.7: And that Iaakob had obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Padan Aram:
28.8: Also Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan displeased Izhak his father,
28.9: Then went Esau to Ishmael, and took unto the wives, which he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abrahams sonne, the sister of Nabaioth, to be his wife.
28.10: Now Iaakob departed from Beer-sheba, and went to Haran,
28.11: And he came unto a certain place, and taried there al night, because the sunne was down, and took of the stones of the place, and layde under his head and slept in the same place.
28.12: Then he dreamed, and behold, there stood a ladder upon the earth, and the top of it reached up to heaven: and loe, the Angels of God went up and down by it.
28.13: And behold, the Lord stood above it, and sayd, I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Izhak: the land, upon the which thou sleepest, wil I give thee and thy seed.
28.14: And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the West, and to the East, and to the North, and to the South, and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
28.15: And lo, I am with thee, and wil keep thee whithersoever thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land: for I will not forsake thee until I have performed that, that I have promised thee.
28.16: Then Iaakob awoke out of his sleep, and sayde, Surely the Lord is in this place, and I was not aware.
28.17: And he was afraid, and said, How fearefull is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
28.18: Then Iaakob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that hee had layde under his head, and set it up as a pillar, and powred oyle upon the top of it.
28.19: And he called ye name of that place Bethel: notwithstanding the name of the citie was at the first called Luz.
28.20: Then Iaakob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this journey which I go, and wil give me bread to eat, and clothes to put on:
28.21: So that I come again unto my fathers house in safetie, then shall the Lord be my God.
28.22: And this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be Gods house: and of all that thou shalt give me, wil I give the tenth unto thee.

29.1: Then Iaakob lift up his feet and came into the East countrey.
29.2: And as he looked about, behold there was a well in the field, and lo, three flocks of sheep lay thereby (for at that well were the flockes watered) and there was a great stone upon the welles mouth.
29.3: And thither were all the flockes gathered, and they rolled the stone from the welles mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the welles mouth in his place.
29.4: And Iaakob sayde unto them, My brethren, whence be ye? And they answered, We are of Haran.
29.5: Then he sayd unto them, Know ye Laban the sonne of Nahor? Who said, We know him.
29.6: Again he sayd unto them, Is he in good health? And they answered, He is in good health, and behold, his daughter Rahel cometh with the sheep.
29.7: Then he sayd, Lo, it is yet hie day, neither is it time that the cattell should be gathered together: water ye the sheep and go feed them.
29.8: But they sayde, We may not until all the flocks be brought together, and till men roll the stone from the welles mouth, that we may water the sheep.
29.9: While he talked with them, Rahel also came with her fathers sheep, for she kept them.
29.10: And assoone as Iaakob saw Rahel ye daughter of Laban his mothers brother, and the sheep of Laban his mothers brother, then came Iaakob neere, and rolled the stone from the welles mouth, and watered ye flock of Laban his mothers brother.
29.11: And Iaakob kissed Rahel, and lift up his voyce and wept.
29.12: (For Iaakob told Rahel, that he was her fathers brother, and that he was Rebekahs sonne) then she ranne and told her father.
29.13: And when Laban heard tell of Iaakob his sisters sonne, he ranne to meet him, and embraced him and kissed him, and brought him to his house: and he told Laban all these things.
29.14: To whom Laban sayd, Well, thou art my bone and my flesh. and he abode with him the space of a moneth.
29.15: For Laban sayde unto Iaakob, Though thou be my brother, shouldest thou therfore serve me for nought? tell me, what shalbe thy wages?
29.16: Now Laban had two daughters, the elder called Leah, and the yonger called Rahel.
29.17: And Leah was tender eyed, but Rahel was beautiful and fair.
29.18: And Iaakob loved Rahel, and sayde, I will serve thee seven yeeres for Rahel thy yonger daughter.
29.19: Then Laban answered, It is better that I give her thee, then that I should give her to another man: abide with me.
29.20: And Iaakob served seven yeres for Rahel, and they seemed unto him but a few dayes, because he loved her.
29.21: Then Iaakob sayde to Laban, Give me my wife, that I may goe in to her: for my terme is ended.
29.22: Wherefore Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
29.23: But whe the evening was come, he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him, and he went in unto her.
29.24: And Laban gave his mayde Zilpah to his daughter Leah, to be her servant.
29.25: But when the morning was come, behold, it was Leah. Then sayde he to Laban, Wherefore hast thou done thus to mee? did not I serve thee for Rahel? wherfore then hast thou beguiled me?
29.26: And Laban answered, It is not the maner of this place, to give the yonger before the elder.
29.27: Fulfil seven yeeres for her, and we wil also give thee this for the service, which thou shalt serve me yet seven yeeres more.
29.28: Then Iaakob did so, and fulfilled her seven yeeres, so he gave him Rahel his daughter to be his wife.
29.29: Laban also gave to Rahel his daughter Bilhah his mayde to be her servant.
29.30: So entred he in to Rahel also, and loved also Rahel more then Leah, and served him yet seven yeeres more.
29.31: When the Lord saw that Leah was despised, he made her fruitful: but Rahel was barren.
29.32: And Leah conceived and bare a sonne, and she called his name Reuben: for she said, Because the Lord hath looked upon my tribulation, now therefore mine husband will love me.
29.33: And she conceived again and bare a sonne, and sayde, Because the Lord heard that I was hated, he hath therefore given me this sonne also, and she called his name Simeon.
29.34: And she conceived again and bare a sonne, and said, Now at this time wil my husband keep mee company, because I have borne him three sonnes: therefore was his name called Levi.
29.35: Moreover she conceived again and bare a sonne, saying, Now will I prayse the Lord: therefore she called his name Judah, and left bearing.

30.1: And when Rahel saw that she bare Iaakob no children, Rahel envied her sister, and said unto Iaakob, Give me children, or els I dye.
30.2: Then Iaakobs anger was kindled against Rahel, and he sayde, Am I in Gods stead, which hath withholden from thee the fruit of the womb?
30.3: And she said, Behold my maid Bilhah, goe in to her, and she shall bear upon my knees, and I shall have children also by her.
30.4: Then she gave him Bilhah her mayde to wife, and Iaakob went in to her.
30.5: So Bilhah conceived and bare Iaakob a sonne.
30.6: Then said Rahel, God hath given sentence on my side, and hath also heard my voyce, and hath given mee a sonne: therefore called she his name, Dan.
30.7: And Bilhah Rahels maid coceiued again, and bare Iaakob the second sonne.
30.8: Then Rahel said, with excellent wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and have gotten the upper hand: and she called his name, Naphtali.
30.9: And when Leah saw that she had left bearing, she took Zilpah her mayde, and gave her Iaakob to wife.
30.10: And Zilpah Leahs mayde bare Iaakob a sonne.
30.11: Then sayd Leah, A companie cometh: and she called his name, Gad.
30.12: Again Zilpah Leahs mayde bare Iaakob another sonne.
30.13: Then sayde Leah, Ah, blessed am I, for the daughters will bless me. and she called his name, Asher.
30.14: Now Reuben went in the dayes of the wheateharuest, and found mandrakes in the field and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then sayde Rahel to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy sonnes mandrakes.
30.15: But she answered her, Is it a small matter for thee to take mine husband, except thou take my sonnes mandrakes also? Then sayde Rahel, Therefore he shall sleep with thee this night for thy sonnes mandrakes.
30.16: And Iaakob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and sayde, Come in to mee, for I have bought and payed for thee with my sonnes mandrakes: and he slept with her that night.
30.17: And God heard Leah and she conceived, and bare unto Iaakob the fift sonne.
30.18: Then said Leah, God hath given me my reward, because I gave my mayde to my husband, and she called his name Issachar.
30.19: After, Leah conceived again, and bare Iaakob the sixt sonne.
30.20: Then Leah said, God hath endued me with a good dowrie: now will mine husband dwell with me, because I have borne him six sonnes: and she called his name Zebulun.
30.21: After that, she bare a daughter, and she called her name Dinah.
30.22: And God remembred Rahel, and God heard her, and opened her womb.
30.23: So she conceived and bare a sonne, and said, God hath taken away my rebuke.
30.24: And she called his name Joseph, saying, The Lord wil give me yet another sonne.
30.25: And assoone as Rahel had borne Joseph, Iaakob said to Laban, Send me away that I may go unto my place and to my countrey.
30.26: Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served thee, and let me go: for thou knowest what service I have done thee.
30.27: To whom Laban answered, If I have now found fauour in thy sight tarie: I have perceived that the Lord hath blessed me for thy sake.
30.28: Also he said, Appoynt unto me thy wages, and I will give it thee.
30.29: But he sayd unto him, Thou knowest, what service I have done thee, and in what taking thy cattell hath been under me.
30.30: For the litle, that thou haddest before I came, is increased into a multitude: and the Lord hath blessed thee by my coming: but now when shall I travel for mine own house also?
30.31: Then he said, What shall I give thee? And Iaakob answered, Thou shalt give mee nothing at all: if thou wilt doe this thing for mee, I will return, feed, and keep thy sheep.
30.32: I wil pass through all thy flockes this day, and separate from them all the sheep with litle spots and great spots, and al black lambes among the sheep, and the great spotted, and litle spotted among the goates: and it shalbe my wages.
30.33: So shall my righteousness answer for me hereafter, when it shall come for my reward before thy face, and every one that hath not litle or great spots among the goates, and black among the sheep, the same shalbe theft with me.
30.34: Then Laban sayde, Goe to, would God it might be according to thy saying.
30.35: Therefore he took out the same day the hee goates that were partie coloured and with great spots, and all the she goates with litle and great spots, and all that had white in them, and all the black among the sheep, and put them in the keeping of his sonnes.
30.36: And hee set three dayes journey between himself and Iaakob. And Iaakob kept the rest of Labans sheep.
30.37: Then Iaakob took rods of green popular, and of hasell, and of the chesnut tree, and pilled white strakes in them, and made the white appear in the rods.
30.38: Then he put the rods, which he had pilled, in the gutters and watering troughes, when the sheep came to drink, before the sheep. (for they were in heat, when they came to drink)
30.39: And the sheep were in heat before the rods, and afterward brought forth yong of partie colour, and with small and great spots.
30.40: And Iaakob parted these lambes, and turned the faces of the flock towardes these lambes partie coloured and all maner of black, among the sheep of Laban: so hee put his own flockes by themselves, and put them not with Labans flock.
30.41: And in every ramming time of the stronger sheep, Iaakob layde the rods before the eyes of the sheep in the gutters, that they might conceive before the rods.
30.42: But when the sheep were feeble, hee put them not in: and so the feebler were Labans, and the stronger Iaakobs.
30.43: So the man increased exceedingly, and had many flockes, and maid seruantes, and men servants, and camels and asses.

31.1: Now he heard the words of Labans sonnes, saying, Iaakob hath taken away all that was our fathers, and of our fathers goods hath he gotten all this honour.
31.2: Also Iaakob beheld the countenance of Laban, that it was not towards him as in times past:
31.3: And the Lord had said unto Iaakob, Turn again into the land of thy fathers, and to thy kinred, and I wilbe with thee.
31.4: Therefore Iaakob sent and called Rahel and Leah to the field unto his flock.
31.5: Then sayde hee unto them, I see your fathers countenance, that it is not towardes me as it was wont, and the God of my father hath been with me.
31.6: And yee know that I have served your father with all my might.
31.7: But your father hath deceived me, and changed my wages tenne times: but God suffred him not to hurt me.
31.8: If he thus sayd, The spotted shall be thy wages, then all the sheep bare spotted: and if he sayd thus, the party coloured shalbe thy reward, then bare all the sheep particoloured.
31.9: Thus hath God taken away your fathers substance, and given it me.
31.10: For in ramming time I lifted up mine eyes and saw in a dream, and behold, ye hee goates leaped upon the she goates, that were partie coloured with litle and great spots spotted.
31.11: And the Angel of God sayde to mee in a dream, Iaakob. And I answered, Lo, I am here.
31.12: And he sayde, Lift up now thine eyes, and see all the hee goates leaping upon ye she goates that are partie coloured, spotted with litle and great spots: for I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee.
31.13: I am the God of Beth-el, where thou anoyntedst the pillar, where thou vowedst a vow unto me. Now arise, get thee out of this countrey and return unto ye land where thou wast borne.
31.14: Then answered Rahel and Leah, and sayde unto him, Have wee any more porcion and inheritance in our fathers house?
31.15: Doeth not he count us as strangers? for he hath sold us, and hath eaten up and consumed our money.
31.16: Therefore all the riches, which God hath taken from our father, is ours and our childrens: now then whatsoever God hath said unto thee, doe it.
31.17: Then Iaakob rose up, and set his sonnes and his wives upon camels.
31.18: And he caried away all his flockes, and al his substance which he had gotten, to wit, his riches, which he had gotten in Padan Aram, to goe to Izhak his father unto the land of Canaan.
31.19: Whe Laban was gone to shere his sheep, Then Rahel stole her fathers idoles.
31.20: Thus Iaakob stole away ye heart of Laban the Aramite: for he told him not that he fled.
31.21: So fled he with all that he had, and he rose up, and passed the river, and set his face toward mount Gilead.
31.22: And the third day after was it told Laban, that Iaakob fled.
31.23: Then he took his brethren with him, and followed after him seven dayes journey, and overtook him at mount Gilead.
31.24: And God came to Laban the Aramite in a dream by night, and sayde unto him, Take heed that thou speak not to Iaakob ought save good.
31.25: Then Laban overtook Iaakob, and Iaakob had pitched his tent in the mount: and Laban also with his brethren pitched upon mount Gilead.
31.26: Then Laban sayde to Iaakob, What hast thou done? thou hast even stolen away mine heart and caried away my daughters as though they had been taken captives with the sword.
31.27: Wherfore diddest thou flie so secretly and steal away from me, and diddest not tel me, that I might have sent thee foorth with mirth and with songs, with timbrel and with harp?
31.28: But thou hast not suffered me to kiss my sonnes and my daughters: now thou hast done foolishly in doing so.
31.29: I am able to do you evil: but the God of your father spake unto me yesternight, saying, Take heed that thou speak not to Iaakob ought save good.
31.30: Now though thou wentest thy way, because thou greatly longedst after thy fathers house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?
31.31: Then Iaakob answered, and said to Laban, Because I was afraid, and thought that thou wouldest have taken thy daughters from me.
31.32: But with whom thou findest thy gods, let him not live. Search thou before our brethre what I have of thine, and take it to thee, (but Iaakob wist not that Rahel had stolen them)
31.33: Then came Laban into Iaakobs tent, and into Leahs tent, and into the two maides tentes, but found them not. So hee went out of Leahs tent, and entred into Rahels tent.
31.34: (Now Rahel had taken the idoles, and put them in the camels litter and sat down upon them) and Laban searched al the tent, but found them not.
31.35: Then said she to her father, My Lord, be not angrie that I cannot rise up before thee: for the custom of women is upon me: so he searched, but found not the idoles.
31.36: The Iaakob was wroth, and chode with Laban: Iaakob also answered and sayd to Laban, What have I trespassed? what have I offended, that thou hast pursued after me?
31.37: Seeing thou hast searched all my stuff, what hast thou foud of all thine houshold stuff? put it here before my brethren and thy brethren, that they may judge between us both.
31.38: This twenty yere I have bin with thee: thine ewes and thy goates have not cast their yong, and the rammes of thy flock have I not eaten.
31.39: Whatsoever was torn of beasts, I brought it not unto thee, but made it good my self: of mine hand diddest thou require it, were it stolen by day or stolen by night.
31.40: I was in the day consumed with heat, and with frost in the night, and my sleep departed from mine eyes.
31.41: Thus have I been twentie yeere in thine house, and served thee fourteen yeeres for thy two daughters, and six yeeres for thy sheep, and thou hast changed my wages tenne times.
31.42: Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Izhak had been with me, surely thou haddest sent me away now emptie: but God beheld my tribulation, and the labour of mine hads, and rebuked thee yester night.
31.43: Then Laban answered, and said unto Iaakob, These daughters are my daughters, and these sonnes are my sonnes, and these sheep are my sheep, and all that thou seest, is mine, and what can I doe this day unto these my daughters, or to their sonnes which they have borne?
31.44: Now therefore come and let us make a covenant, I and thou, which may be a witnes between me and thee.
31.45: Then took Iaakob a stone, and set it up as a pillar:
31.46: And Iaakob sayde unto his brethren, Gather stones: who brought stones, and made an heap, and they did eat there upon the heap.
31.47: And Laban called it Iegar-sahadutha, and Iaakob called it Galeed.
31.48: For Laban sayd, This heap is witness between me and thee this day: therefore he called the name of it Galeed.
31.49: Also he called it Mizpah, because he said, The Lord look between me and thee, when we shalbe departed one from another,
31.50: If thou shalt vex my daughters, or shalt take wives beside my daughters: there is no man with us, behold, God is witness between me and thee.
31.51: Moreover Laban sayd to Iaakob, Behold this heap, and behold the pillar, which I have set between me and thee,
31.52: This heap shall be witness, and the pillar shall be witness, that I will not come over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar unto me for evil.
31.53: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nabor, and the God of their father be judge between us: But Iaakob sware by the fear of his father Izhak.
31.54: Then Iaakob did offer a sacrifice upon the mount, and called his brethren to eat bread. and they did eat bread, and taried all night in the mount.
31.55: And earely in the morning Laban rose up and kissed his sonnes and his daughters, and blessed them, and Laban departing, went unto his place again.

32.1: Now Iaakob went forth on his journey and the Angels of God met him.
32.2: And when Iaakob saw them, he said, This is Gods host, and called the name of the same place Mahanaim.
32.3: Then Iaakob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother, unto the land of Seir into the countrey of Edom:
32.4: To whom he gave commandement, saying, Thus shall ye speak to my lord Esau: thy servant Iaakob sayeth thus, I have been a stranger with Laban, and taried unto this time.
32.5: I have beeves also and Asses, sheep, and men seruantes, and women seruantes, and have sent to shew my lord, that I may find grace in thy sight.
32.6: So ye messengers came again to Iaakob, saying, We came unto thy brother Esau, and hee also cometh against thee and four hundreth men with him.
32.7: Then Iaakob was greatly afraid, and was sore troubled, and deuided the people that was with him, and the sheep, and the beeves, and the camels into two companies.
32.8: For he said, If Esau come to ye one company and smite it, the other companie shall escape.
32.9: Moreover Iaakob said, O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Izhak: Lord, which saydest unto me, Return unto thy coutrey and to thy kinred, and I will do thee good,
32.10: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies, and al the trueth, which thou hast shewed unto thy servant: for with my staff came I over this Iorden, and now have I gotte two bads.
32.11: I pray thee, Deliver me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, least he will come and smite me, and the mother upon the children.
32.12: For thou saydest; I will surely doe thee good, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which can not be nombred for multitude.
32.13: And he taryed there the same night, and took of that which came to had, a present for Esau his brother:
32.14: Two hundreth she goates and twenty hee goates, two hundreth ewes and twentie rammes:
32.15: Thirtie mylche camels with their coltes, fourtie kine, and ten bullockes, twentie she asses and ten foles.
32.16: So he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by themselves, and said unto his servants, Pass before me, and put a space between drove and drove.
32.17: And he commanded the formost, saying, If Esau my brother meet thee, and ask thee, saying, Whose servant art thou? And whither goest thou? And whose are these before thee?
32.18: Then thou shalt say, They be thy servant Iaakobs: it is a present sent unto my lord Esau: and behold, he him self also is behind us.
32.19: So likewise commanded he the second and the third, and all that followed the droves, saying, After this maner, ye shall speak unto Esau, when ye find him.
32.20: And ye shall say moreover, Behold, thy servant Iaakob cometh after us (for he thought, I will appease his wrath with the present that goeth before me, and afterward I will see his face: it may be that he will accept me.)
32.21: So went the present before him: but he taried that night with the companie.
32.22: And he rose up the same night, and took his two wives, and his two maides, and his eleven children, and went over the ford Jabbok.
32.23: And he took them, and sent them over the river, and sent over that he had.
32.24: Now when Iaakob was left him self alone, there wrestled a man with him unto the breaking of the day.
32.25: And he saw that he could not prevail against him: therefore he touched the holowe of his thigh, and the holowe of Iaakobs thigh was loosed, as he wrestled with him.
32.26: And he said, Let me goe, for the morning appeareth. Who answered, I will not let thee go except thou bless me.
32.27: Then said he unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Iaakob.
32.28: Then said he, Thy name shalbe called Iaakob no more, but Israel: because thou hast had power with God, thou shalt also prevail with men.
32.29: Then Iaakob demaded, saying, Tell me, I pray thee, thy name. And he said, Wherefore now doest thou ask my name? and he blessed him there
32.30: And Iaakob called the name of the place, Peniel: for, said he, I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.
32.31: And the sunne rose up to him as he passed Peniel, and he halted upon his thigh.
32.32: Therefore the children of Israel eat not of the sinew that shrank in the hollow of the thigh, unto this day: because he touched the sinew that shrank in the holow of Iaakobs thigh.

33.1: And as Iaakob lift up his eyes, and looked, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundreth men: and he deuided the children to Leah, and to Rahel, and to the two maides.
33.2: And he put the maides, and their children formost, and Leah, and her children after, and Rahel, and Joseph hindermost.
33.3: So he went before them and bowed him self to the ground seven times, until he came neere to his brother.
33.4: Then Esau ranne to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him, and they wept.
33.5: And he lift up his eyes, and saw the women, and the children, and said, Who are these with thee? And he answered, They are ye childre whom God of his grace hath given thy servant.
33.6: Then came the maides neere, they, and their children, and bowed themselves.
33.7: Leah also with her children came neere and made obeysance: and after Joseph and Rahel drew neere, and did reverence.
33.8: Then he said, What meanest thou by all this drove, which I met? Who answered, I have sent it, that I may find fauour in the sight of my lord:
33.9: And Esau said, I have ynough, my brother: keep that thou hast to thy self.
33.10: But Iaakob answered, Nay, I pray thee: if I have found grace now in thy sight, then receive my present at mine hand: for I have seen thy face, as though I had seen the face of God, because thou hast accepted me.
33.11: I pray thee take my blessing, that is brought thee: for God hath had mercie on me, and therefore I have all things: so he compelled him, and he took it.
33.12: And he said, Let us take our journey and go, and I will goe before thee.
33.13: Then he answered him, My lord knoweth, that the children are tender, and the ewes and kine with yong under mine hand: and if they should overdrive them one day, all the flock would die.
33.14: Let now my lord go before his servant, and I will drive softly, according to ye pase of ye cattel, which is before me, and as the children be able to endure, until I come to my lord unto Seir.
33.15: Then Esau said, I will leave then some of my folk with thee. And he answered, what needeth this? let me find grace in the sight of my lord.
33.16: So Esau returned, and went his way that same day unto Seir.
33.17: And Iaakob went forward toward Succoth, and built him an house, and made boothes for his cattell: therefore he called the name of the place Succoth.
33.18: Afterward, Iaakob came safe to Sheche a citie, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan Aram, and pitched before the citie.
33.19: And there he bought a parcel of ground, where hee pitched his tent, at the hand of the sonnes of Hamor Shechems father, for an hundreth pieces of money.
33.20: And he set up there an altar, and called it, The mightie God of Israel.

34.1: Then Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Iaakob, went out to see the daughters of that countrey.
34.2: Whom when Shechem the sonne of Hamor the Hivite lord of that countrey saw, hee took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.
34.3: So his heart clave unto Dinah the daughter of Iaakob: and he loved the maid, and spake kindely unto the maid.
34.4: Then said Shechem to his father Hamor, saying, Get me this maid to wife.
34.5: (Now Iaakob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter, and his sonnes were with his cattell in the field: therefore Iaakob held his peace, until they were come.)
34.6: Then Hamor the father of Shechem went out unto Iaakob to commune with him.
34.7: And whe the sonnes of Iaakob were come out of the field and heard it, it grieved the men, and they were very angry, because he had wrought villenie in Israel, in that he had lyen with Iaakobs daughter: which thing ought not to be done.
34.8: And Hamor communed with them, saying, the soul of my sonne Shechem longeth for your daughter: give her him to wife, I pray you.
34.9: So make affinitie with us: give your daughters unto us, and take our daughters unto you,
34.10: And ye shall dwell with us, and the land shalbe before you: dwell, and doe your business in it, and have your possessions therein.
34.11: Shechem also said unto her father and unto her brethren, Let me find fauour in your eyes, and I will give whatsoever ye shall appoint me.
34.12: Ask of me abundantly both dowrie and giftes, and I will give as ye appoint me, so that ye give me the maid to wife.
34.13: Then the sonnes of Iaakob answered Shechem and Hamor his father, talking deceitfully, because he had defiled Dinah their sister,
34.14: And they said unto them, We can not do this thing, to give our sister to an uncircumcised man: for that were a reproof unto us.
34.15: But in this will we consent unto you, if ye will be as we are, that every man child among you be circumcised:
34.16: Then will we give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters to us, and will dwell with you, and be one people.
34.17: But if ye will not hearken unto us to be circumcised, then will we take our daughter and depart.
34.18: Now their wordes pleased Hamor, and Shechem Hamors sonne.
34.19: And the yong man deferd not to doe the thing because he loved Iaakobs daughter: he was also the most set by of all his fathers house.
34.20: Then Hamor and Shechem his Sonne went unto the gate of their citie, and communed with the men of their citie, saying,
34.21: These men are peaceable with us: and that they may dwell in the land, and doe their affaires therin (for behold, the land hath roume ynough for them) let us take their daughters to wives, and give them our daughters.
34.22: Onely herein will the men consent unto us for to dwell with us, and to be one people, if all the men children among us be circumcised as they are circumcised.
34.23: Shall not their flockes and their substance and all their cattell be ours? onely let us consent herein unto them, and they will dwell with us.
34.24: And unto Hamor, and Shechem his sonne hearkened all that went out of the gate of his citie: and all the men children were circumcised, even all that went out of the gate of his citie.
34.25: And on the third day (when they were sore) two of the sonnes of Iaakob, Simeon and Levi, Dinahs brethren took either of them his sword and went into the citie boldly, and slue every male.
34.26: They slew also Hamor and Shechem his sonne with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechems house, and went their way.
34.27: Again the other sonnes of Iaakob came upon the dead, and spoyled the citie, because they had defiled their sister.
34.28: They took their sheep and their beeves, and their asses, and whatsoever was in the citie, and in the fieldes.
34.29: Also they caryed away captive and spoyled all their goods, and all their children and their wives, and all that was in the houses.
34.30: Then Iaakob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me, and made me stink among the inhabitats of the land, aswell the Canaanites, as the Perizzites, and and I being few in nomber, they shall gather theselues together against me, and slay me, and so shall I, and my house be destroied.
34.31: And they answered, Should hee abuse our sister as a whore?

35.1: Then God sayde to Iaakob, Arise, goe up to Beth-el and dwell there, and make there an altar unto God, that appeared unto thee, when thou fleddest from Esau thy brother.
35.2: Then said Iaakob unto his houshold and to all that were with him, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and clense your selves, and change your garments:
35.3: For we will rise and goe up to Beth-el, and I will make an altar there unto God, which heard me in the day of my tribulation, and was with me in the way which I went.
35.4: And they gave unto Iaakob all the strange gods, which were in their hands, and all their earings which were in their eares, and Iaakob hid them under an oke, which was by Shechem.
35.5: Then they went on their journey, and the fear of God was upon the cities that were roud about them: so that they did not follow after the sonnes of Iaakob.
35.6: So came Iaakob to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan: (the same is Beth-el) hee and all the people that was with him.
35.7: And he built there an altar, and had called the place, The God of Beth-el, because that God appeared unto him there, when he fled from his brother.
35.8: Then Deborah Rebekahs nourse dyed, and was buried beneath Beth-el under an oke: and he called the name of it Allon Bachuth.
35.9: Again God appeared unto Iaakob, after he came out of Padan Aram, and blessed him.
35.10: Moreover God said unto him, Thy name is Iaakob: thy name shalbe no more called Iaakob, but Israel shalbe thy name: and hee called his name Israel.
35.11: Again God said unto him, I am God all sufficient. grow, and multiplie. a nation and a multitude of nations shall spring of thee, and Kings shall come out of thy loynes.
35.12: Also I will give the land, which I gave to Abraham and Izhak, unto thee: and unto thy seed after thee will I give that land.
35.13: So God ascended from him in the place where he had talked with him.
35.14: And Iaakob set up a pillar in the place where he talked with him, a pillar of stone, and powred drink offring thereon: also hee powred oyle thereon.
35.15: And Iaakob called the name of the place, where God spake with him, Beth-el.
35.16: Then they departed from Beth-el, and when there was about half a daies journey of ground to come to Ephrath, Rahel travailed, and in travailing she was in peril.
35.17: And whe she was in paines of her labour, the midwife said unto her, Fear not: for thou shalt have this sonne also.
35.18: Then as she was about to yeelde up the Ghost (for she died) she called his name Ben-oni, but his father called him Beniamin.
35.19: Thus died Rahel, and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Beth-lehem.
35.20: And Iaakob set a pillar upon her grave: This is the pillar of Rahels grave unto this day.
35.21: Then Israel went forward, and pitched his tent beyond Migdal-eder.
35.22: Now, when Israel dwelt in that land, Reuben went, and lay with Bilhah his fathers concubine, and it came to Israels ear. And Iaakob had twelve sonnes.
35.23: The sonnes of Leah: Reuben Iaakobs eldest sonne, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun.
35.24: The sonnes of Rahel: Joseph and Beniamin.
35.25: And the sonnes of Bilhah Rahels maid: Dan and Naphtali.
35.26: And the sonnes of Zilpah Leahs maid: Gad and Asher. These are the sonnes of Iaakob, which were borne him in Padan Aram.
35.27: Then Iaakob came unto Izhak his father to Mamre a citie of Arbah: this is Hebron, where Abraham and Izhak were strangers.
35.28: And the daies of Izhak were an hundreth and fourescore yeeres.
35.29: And Izhak gave up the ghost and died, and was gathered unto his people, being old and full of daies: and his sonnes Esau and Iaakob buried him.

36.1: Now these are the generations of Esau, which is Edom.
36.2: Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon an Hittite, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon an Hivite,
36.3: And took Basemath Ishmaels daughter, sister of Nebaioth.
36.4: And Adah bare unto Esau, Eliphaz: and Basemath bare Reuel.
36.5: Also Aholibamah bare Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah: these are the sonnes of Esau which were borne to him in the land of Canaan.
36.6: So Esau took his wives and his sonnes, and his daughters, and all the soules of his house, and his flocks, and all his cattell, and all his substance, which he had gotten in the land of Canaan, and went into an other countrey from his brother Iaakob.
36.7: For their riches were so great, that they could not dwell together, and the land, wherein they were strangers, could not receive them because of their flockes.
36.8: Therefore dwelt Esau in mount Seir: this Esau is Edom.
36.9: So these are the generations of Esau father of Edom in mount Seir.
36.10: These are the names of Esaus sonnes: Eliphaz, the sonne of Adah, the wife of Esau, and Reuel the sonne of Bashemath, the wife of Esau.
36.11: And the sonnes of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
36.12: And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esaus sonne, and bare unto Eliphaz, Amalek: these be the sonnes of Adah Esaus wife.
36.13: And these are the sonnes of Reuel: Nahath, and Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah: these were the sonnes of Bashemath Esaus wife.
36.14: And these were the sonnes of Aholibamah the daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon Esaus wife: for she bare unto Esau, Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah.
36.15: These were Dukes of the sonnes of Esau: the sonnes of Eliphaz, the first borne of Esau: Duke Teman, Duke Omar, Duke Zepho, Duke Kenaz,
36.16: Duke Korah, Duke Gatam, Duke Amalek: these are the Dukes that came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom: these were the sonnes of Adah.
36.17: And these are the sonnes of Reuel Esaus sonne: Duke Nahath, Duke Zerah, Duke Shammah, Duke Mizzah: these are the Dukes that came of Reuel in the land of Edom: these are the sonnes of Bashemath Esaus wife.
36.18: Likewise these were the sonnes of Aholibamah Esaus wife: Duke Jeush, Duke Jaalam, Duke Korah: these Dukes came of Aholibamah, the daughter of Anah Esaus wife.
36.19: These are the children of Esau, and these are the Dukes of them: This Esau is Edom.
36.20: These are the sonnes of Seir the Horite, which inhabited the land before, Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah.
36.21: And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these are the Dukes of the Horites, the sonnes of Seir in the land of Edom.
36.22: And the sonnes of Lotan were, Hori and Hemam, and Lotans sister was Timna.
36.23: And the sonnes of Shobal were these: Alvan, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
36.24: And these are the sonnes of Zibeon: Both Aiah, and Anah: this was Anah that found mules in the wilderness, as he fedde his father Zibeons asses.
36.25: And the children of Anah were these: Dishon and Aholibamah, the daughter of Anah.
36.26: Also these are the sonnes of Dishan: Hemdan, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
36.27: The sonnes of Ezer are these: Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan.
36.28: The sonnes of Dishan are these: Uz, and Aran.
36.29: These are the Dukes of the Horites: Duke Lotan, Duke Shobal, Duke Zibeon, Duke Anah,
36.30: Duke Dishon, Duke Ezer, Duke Dishan: these bee the Dukes of the Horites, after their Dukedomes in the land of Seir.
36.31: And these are the Kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any King over the children of Israel.
36.32: Then Bela the sonne of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his citie was Dinhabah.
36.33: And when Bela dyed, Jobab the sonne of Zerah of Bozra reigned in his stead.
36.34: When Jobab also was dead, Husham of the land of Temani reigned in his stead.
36.35: And after the death of Husham, Hadad the sonne of Bedad, which slew Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead, and the name of his citie was Avith.
36.36: When Hadad was dead, then Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.
36.37: When Samlah was dead, Shaul of Rehoboth by the river, reigned in his stead.
36.38: When Shaul dyed, Baal-hanan the sonne of Achbor reigned in his stead.
36.39: And after the death of Baal-hanan the sonne of Achbor, Hadad reigned in his stead, and the name of his citie was Pau: and his wives name Mehetabel the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
36.40: Then these are the names of the Dukes of Esau according to their families, their places and by their names: Duke Timna, Duke Alvah, Duke Jetheth,
36.41: Duke Aholibamah, Duke Elah, Duke Pinon,
36.42: Duke Kenaz, Duke Teman, Duke Mibzar,
36.43: Duke Magdiel, Duke Iram: these bee the Dukes of Edom, according to their habitations, in the land of their inheritance. This Esau is the father of Edom.

37.1: Iaakob now dwelt in the land, wherein his father was a stranger, in the land of Canaan.
37.2: These are the generations of Iaakob, when Joseph was seventeen yeere old: he kept sheep with his brethren, and the child was with the sonnes of Bilhah, and with the sonnes of Zilpah, his fathers wives. And Joseph brought unto their father their evil saying.
37.3: Now Israel loved Joseph more then all his sonnes, because he begat him in his old age, and he made him a coat of many colours.
37.4: So when his brethren saw that their father loved him more then all his brethren, then they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.
37.5: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and told his brethren, who hated him so much the more.
37.6: For he said unto them, Hear, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed.
37.7: Behold now, wee were binding sheues in the middes of the field: and loe, my shefe arose and also stood upright, and behold, your sheues compassed round about, and did reverence to my shefe.
37.8: Then his brethren said to him, What, shalt thou reign over us, and rule us? or shalt thou have altogether dominion over us? And they hated him so much the more, for his dreames, and for his wordes.
37.9: Again hee dreamed an other dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have had one dream more, and behold, the Sunne and the Moon and eleven starres did reverence to me.
37.10: Then he told it unto his father and to his brethren, and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream, which thou hast dreamed? shall I, and thy mother, and thy brethren come in deed and fall on the ground before thee?
37.11: And his brethren envied him, but his father noted the saying.
37.12: Then his brethren went to keep their fathers sheep in Shechem.
37.13: And Israel said unto Joseph, Doe not thy brethren keep in Shechem? come and I will send thee to them.
37.14: And he answered him, I am here. Then he said unto him, Goe now, see whether it bee well with thy brethren, and how the flocks prosper, and bring me word again. so hee sent him from the vale of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
37.15: Then a man found him: for lo, hee was wandring in the field, and the man asked him, saying, What seekest thou?
37.16: And he answered, I seek my brethren: tell me, I pray thee, where they keep sheep.
37.17: And the man said, they are departed hece: for I heard them say, Let us goe unto Dothan. Then went Joseph after his brethren, and found them in Dothan.
37.18: And when they saw him a far off, even before he came at them, they conspired against him for to slay him.
37.19: For they sayd one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh.
37.20: Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pitte, and wee will say, A wicked beast hath deuoured him: then wee shall see, what will come of his dreames.
37.21: But when Reuben heard that, he delivered him out of their handes, and said, Let us not kill him.
37.22: Also Reuben said unto them, Shed not blood, but cast him into this pitte that is in the wilderness, and lay no hand upon him. Thus he said, that he might deliver him out of their hand, and restore him to his father again.
37.23: Now when Joseph was come unto his brethren, they stript Joseph out of his coat, his particoloured coat that was upon him.
37.24: And they took him, and cast him into a pit, and the pit was emptie, without water in it.
37.25: Then they sat them down to eat bread: and they lift up their eyes and looked, and behold, there came a companie of Ishmeelites from Gilead, and their camels laden with spicerie, and balm, and myrrh, and were going to cary it down into Egypt.
37.26: Then Judah said unto his brethren, What availeth it, if we slay our brother, though wee keep his blood secret?
37.27: Come and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our handes be upon him: for he is our brother and our flesh: and his brethren obeyed.
37.28: Then the Midianites marchant men passed by, and they drew foorth, and lift Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph unto the Ishmeelites for twentie pieces of silver: who brought Joseph into Egypt.
37.29: Afterward Reuben returned to the pit, and behold, Joseph was not in the pit: then he rent his clothes,
37.30: And returned to his brethren, and said, The child is not yonder, and I, whither shall I goe?
37.31: And they took Iosephs coat, and killed a kidde of the goates, and dipped the coat in the blood.
37.32: So they sent that particoloured coat, and they brought it unto their father, and said, This have we found: see now, whether it be thy sonnes coat, or no.
37.33: Then he knew it and said, It is my sonnes coat: a wicked beast hath deuoured him: Joseph is surely torn in pieces.
37.34: And Iaakob rent his clothes, and put sackecloth about his loynes, and sorowed for his sonne a long season.
37.35: Then all his sonnes and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he would not be comforted, but said, Surely I will go down into the grave unto my sonne mourning: so his father wept for him.
37.36: And the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar an Eunuch of Pharaohs, and his chief steward.

38.1: And at that time Judah went down from his brethren, and turned in to a man called Hirah an Adullamite.
38.2: And Judah saw there the daughter of a man called Suah a Canaanite: and he took her to wife, and went in unto her.
38.3: So she conceived and bare a sonne, and he called his name Er.
38.4: And she conceived again, and bare a sonne, and she called his name Onan.
38.5: Moreover she bare yet a sonne, whom she called Shelah: and Judah was at Chezib when she bare him.
38.6: Then Judah took a wife to Er his first borne sonne whose name was Tamar.
38.7: Now Er the first borne of Judah was wicked in the sight of the Lord: therefore the Lord slew him.
38.8: Then Judah said to Onan, Goe in unto thy brothers wife, and do the office of a kinsman unto her, and raise up seed unto thy brother.
38.9: And Onan knew that the seed should not be his: therefore when he went in unto his brothers wife, he spilled it on the ground, least he should give seed unto his brother.
38.10: And it was wicked in the eyes of the Lord, which he did: wherefore he slew him also.
38.11: Then said Judah to Tamar his daughter in law, Remain a widow in thy fathers house, till Shelah my sonne grow up (for he thought thus, Least he die as well as his brethren.) So Tamar went and dwelt in her fathers house.
38.12: And in process of time also the daughter of Shuah Iudahs wife dyed. Then Judah, when he had left mourning, went up to his sheep sherers to Timnah, he, and his neighbour Hirah the Adullamite.
38.13: And it was told Tamar, saying, behold, thy father in law goeth up to Timnah, to shere his sheep.
38.14: Then she put her widowes garments off from her, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped her self, and sat down in Pethah-enaim, which is by the way to Timnah, because she saw that Shelah was growen, and she was not given unto him to wife.
38.15: When Judah saw her, he judged her an whore: for she had covered her face.
38.16: And he turned to the way towardes her, and said, Come, I pray thee, let me lie with thee. (for he knew not that she was his daughter in law) And she answered, What wilt thou give me for to lie with me?
38.17: Then said he, I will send thee a kid of the goates from the flock. and she said, Well, if thou wilt give me a pledge, till thou send it.
38.18: Then he said, What is the pledge that I shall give thee? And she answered, Thy signet, and thy cloke, and thy staff that is in thine hand. So he gave it her, and lay by her, and she was with child by him.
38.19: Then she rose, and went and put her vail from her and put on her widowes raiment.
38.20: Afterward Judah sent a kid of the goates by the hand of his neighbour the Adullamite, for to receive his pledge from the womans hand: but he found her not.
38.21: Then asked he the men of that place, saying, Where is ye whore, that sat in Enaim by the way side? And they answered, There was no whore here.
38.22: He came therefore to Judah again, and said, I can not find her, and also the men of the place said, There was no whore there.
38.23: Then Judah said, Let her take it to her, lest we be shamed: behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.
38.24: Now after three moneths, one told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter in law hath played the whore, and lo, with playing the whore, she is great with child. Then Judah said, Bring ye her foorth and let her be burnt.
38.25: When she was brought foorth, she sent to her father in law, saying, By the man, unto whom these things pertain, am I with child: and said also, Look, I pray thee, whose these are, the seal, and the cloke, and the staff.
38.26: Then Judah knew them, and said, She is more righteous then I: for she hath done it because I gave her not to Shelah my sonne. So he lay with her no more.
38.27: Now, when the time was come that she should be delivered, behold, there were twinnes in her womb.
38.28: And when she was in travel, the one put out his hand: and the midwife took and bound a red threde about his hand, saying, This is come out first.
38.29: But when he plucked his hand back again, loe, his brother came out, and the midwife said, How hast thou broken the breach upon thee? and his name was called Pharez.
38.30: And afterward came out his brother that had the red threde about his hand, and his name was called Zarah.

39.1: Now Joseph was brought down into Egypt: and Potiphar an Eunuch of Pharaohs (and his chief steward an Egyptian) bought him at the hand of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him thither.
39.2: And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a man that prospered and was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
39.3: And his master saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that hee did to prosper in his hand.
39.4: So Joseph found fauour in his sight, and served him: and he made him ruler of his house, and put all that he had in his hand.
39.5: And from that time that he had made him ruler over his house and over all that he had, the Lord blessed the Egyptians house for Iosephs sake: and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.
39.6: Therefore he left all that he had in Iosephs hand, and took accompt of nothing, that was with him, save onely of the bread, which he did eat. And Joseph was a fair person, and well fauoured.
39.7: Now therefore after these thinges, his masters wife cast her eyes upon Joseph, and said, Lye with me.
39.8: But he refused and said to his masters wife, Behold, my master knoweth not what he hath in the house with me, but hath committed all that he hath to mine hand.
39.9: There is no man greater in this house then I: neither hath he kept any thing from me, but only thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickednes and so sinne against God?
39.10: And albeit she spake to Joseph day by day, yet he hearkened not unto her, to lye with her, or to be in her company.
39.11: Then on a certain day Joseph entred into the house, to doe his business: and there was no man of the houshold in the house:
39.12: Therefore she caught him by his garmet, saying, Sleep with me: but he left his garment in her hand and fled, and got him out.
39.13: Now when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled out,
39.14: She called unto the men of her house, and told them, saying, Behold, he hath brought in an Ebrewe unto us to mock us: who came in to me for to have slept with me: but I cryed with a loud voyce.
39.15: And when he heard that I lift up my voice and cryed, he left his garment with me, and fled away, and got him out.
39.16: So she layde up his garment by her, until her lord came home.
39.17: Then she told him according to these words, saying, The Ebrew seruat, which thou hast brought unto us, came in to me, to mock me.
39.18: But assoone as I lift up my voyce and cried, he left his garment with me, and fled out.
39.19: Then when his master heard the wordes of his wife, which she told him, saying, After this maner did thy servant to me, his anger was kindled.
39.20: And Iosephs master took him and put him in prison, in the place, where the kings prisoners lay bound: and there he was in prison.
39.21: But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercie, and got him fauour in the sight of the master of the prison.
39.22: And the keeper of the prison committed to Iosephs hand all the prisoners that were in the prison, and whatsoever they did there, that did he.
39.23: And the keeper of the prison looked unto nothing that was under his hand, seeing that the Lord was with him: for whatsoever he did, the Lord made it to prosper.

40.1: And after these things, the butler of the King of Egypt and his baker offended their lord the King of Egypt.
40.2: And Pharaoh was angrie against his two officers, against the chief butler, and against the chief baker.
40.3: Therefore he put them in ward in his chief stewardes house, in the prison and place where Joseph was bound.
40.4: And the chief steward gave Joseph charge over them, and he served them: and they continued a season in ward.
40.5: And they both dreamed a dream, eyther of them his dream in one night, eche one according to the interpretation of his dream, both the butler and the baker of the King of Egypt, which were bound in the prison.
40.6: And when Joseph came in unto them in the morning, and looked upon them, behold, they were sad.
40.7: And he asked Pharaohs officers, that were with him in his masters ward, saying, Wherefore look ye so sadly to day?
40.8: Who answered him, We have dreamed, eche one a dream, and there is none to interpret the same. Then Joseph said unto them, Are not interpretations of God? tell them me now.
40.9: So the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, and said unto him, In my dream, behold, a vine was before me,
40.10: And in the vine were three branches, and as it budded, her flowre came foorth: and the clusters of grapes waxed ripe.
40.11: And I had Pharaohs cup in mine hand, and I took the grapes, and wrung the into Pharaohs cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaohs hand.
40.12: Then Joseph sayde unto him, This is the interpretation of it: The three braunches are three dayes.
40.13: Within three dayes shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thine office, and thou shalt give Pharaohs cup into his hand after the old maner, when thou wast his butler.
40.14: But have me in remembrance with thee, when thou art in good case, and shew mercie, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring me out of this house.
40.15: For I was stolen away by theft out of the land of the Ebrewes, and here also have I done nothing, wherefore they should put mee in the dungeon.
40.16: And when the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, hee said unto Joseph, Also mee thought in my dream that I had three white baskets on mine head.
40.17: And in the uppermost basket there was of all maner baken meates for Pharaoh: and the birdes did eat them out of the basket upon mine head.
40.18: Then Joseph answered, and said, This is the interpretation thereof: The three baskets are three dayes:
40.19: Within three dayes shall Pharaoh take thine head from thee, and shall hang thee on a tree, and the birdes shall eat thy flesh from off thee.
40.20: And so the third day, which was Pharaohs birthday, hee made a feast unto all his servants: and hee lifted up the head of the chief butler, and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
40.21: And he restored the chief butler unto his butlershippe, who gave the cup into Pharaohs hand,
40.22: But he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted unto them.
40.23: Yet the chief butler did not remember Joseph, but forgat him.

41.1: And two yeeres after, Pharaoh also dreamed, and behold, he stood by a river,
41.2: And loe, there came out of the river seven goodly kine and fatfleshed, and they fedde in a medowe:
41.3: And loe, seven other kine came up after the out of the river, evil fauoured and lean fleshed, and stood by the other kine upon the brink of the river.
41.4: And the euilfauoured and lean fleshed kine did eat up the seven welfauoured and fatte kine: so Pharaoh awoke.
41.5: Again he slept, and dreamed the second time: and behold, seven eares of corn grew upon one stalk, rank and goodly.
41.6: And loe, seven thin eares, and blasted with the east wind, sprang up after them:
41.7: And the thin eares deuoured the seven rank and full eares. then Pharaoh awaked, and loe, it was a dream.
