41.8: Now when the morning came, his spirit was troubled: therefore he sent and called all the soothsayers of Egypt, and all the wise men thereof, and Pharaoh told them his dreames: but none could interpret them to Pharaoh.
41.9: Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I call to mind my faultes this day.
41.10: Pharaoh being angrie with his seruantes, put me in ward in the chief stewards house, both me and the chief baker.
41.11: Then we dreamed a dream in one night, both I, and he: we dreamed eche man according to the interpretation of his dream.
41.12: And there was with us a yong man, an Ebrew, servant unto the chief steward, whom when we told, he declared our dreames to us, to every one he declared according to his dream.
41.13: And as he declared unto us, so it came to pass: for he restored me to mine office, and hanged him.
41.14: Then sent Pharaoh, and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of prison, and he shaved him, and chaunged his rayment, and came to Pharaoh.
41.15: Then Pharaoh sayde to Joseph, I have dreamed a dream, and no man can interpret it, and I have heard say of thee, that when thou hearest a dream, thou canst interpret it.
41.16: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, Without me God shall answer for the wealth of Pharaoh.
41.17: And Pharaoh sayde unto Joseph, In my dream, behold, I stood by the bank of the river:
41.18: And lo, there came up out of the river seven fat fleshed, and welfauoured kine, and they fedde in the medowe.
41.19: Also loe, seven other kine came up after them, poor and very euilfauoured, and leanefleshed: I never saw the like in all the land of Egypt, for euilfauoured.
41.20: And the lean and euilfauoured kine did eat up the first seven fat kine.
41.21: And when they had eaten them up, it could not be knowen that they had eaten them, but they were still as euilfauoured, as they were at the beginning: so did I awake.
41.22: Moreover I saw in my dream, and behold, seven eares sprang out of one stalk, full and fair.
41.23: And lo, seven eares, withered, thin, and blasted with the East wind, sprang up after them.
41.24: And the thin eares deuoured the seven good eares. Now I have told the soothsayers, and none can declare it unto me.
41.25: Then Joseph answered Pharaoh, Both Pharaohs dreames are one. God hath shewed Pharaoh, what he is about to doe.
41.26: The seven good kine are seven yeres, and the seven good eares are seven yeeres: this is one dream.
41.27: Likewise the seven thin and euilfauoured kine, that came out after them, are seven yeeres: and the seven emptie eares blasted with the East wind, are seven yeeres of famine.
41.28: This is the thing which I have said unto Pharaoh, that God hath shewed unto Pharaoh, what he is about to doe.
41.29: Behold, there come seven yeeres of great plentie in all the land of Egypt.
41.30: Again, there shall arise after them seven yeeres of famine, so that all the plentie shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt, and the famine shall consume the land:
41.31: Neither shall the plentie bee knowen in the land, by reason of this famine that shall come after: for it shalbe exceeding great.
41.32: And therefore the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh the second time, because the thing is established by God, and God hasteth to perform it.
41.33: Now therefore let Pharaoh provide for a man of understanding and wisedome, and set him over the land of Egypt.
41.34: Let Pharaoh make and appoynt officers over the land, and take up the fift part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous yeeres.
41.35: Also let them gather all the food of these good yeeres that come, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh for food, in the cities, and let them keep it.
41.36: So the food shall be for the provision of the land, against the seven yeeres of famine, which shalbe in the land of Egypt, that the land perish not by famine.
41.37: And the saying pleased Pharaoh and all his servants.
41.38: Then said Pharaoh unto his servants, Can we find such a man as this, in whom is the Spirit of God?
41.39: The Pharaoh said to Joseph, For as much as God hath shewed thee all this, there is no man of understanding, or of wisedome like unto thee.
41.40: Thou shalt be over mine house, and at thy word shall all my people be armed, onely in the kings throne will I be above thee.
41.41: Moreover Pharaoh said to Joseph, Behold, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
41.42: And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Iosephs hand, and arayed him in garments of fine linen, and put a golden cheyne about his neck.
41.43: So he set him upon the best charet that hee had, save one: and they cryed before him, Abrech, and placed him over all the land of Egypt.
41.44: Again Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I am Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.
41.45: And Pharaoh called Iosephs name Zaphnath-paaneah: and he gave him to wife Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah prince of On. then went Joseph abrode in the land of Egypt.
41.46: And Joseph was thirtie yeere old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt: and Joseph departing from the presence of Pharaoh, went throughout all the land of Egypt.
41.47: And in the seven plenteous yeres the earth brought foorth store.
41.48: And hee gathered up all the food of the seven plenteous yeeres, which were in the land of Egypt, and layde up food in the cities: the food of the field, that was round about every citie, layde he up in the same.
41.49: So Joseph gathered wheat, like unto the sand of the sea in multitude out of measure, until he left numbring: for it was without number.
41.50: Now unto Joseph were borne two sonnes (before the yeeres of famine came) which Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah prince of On bare unto him.
41.51: And Joseph called the name of the first borne Manasseh: for God, said he, hath made me forget all my labour and al my fathers houshold.
41.52: Also hee called the name of the second, Ephraim: For God, sayde he hath made me fruitful in the land of mine affliction.
41.53: So the seven yeeres of the plentie that was in the land of Egypt were ended.
41.54: Then began the seven yeeres of famine to come, according as Joseph had said: and the famine was in all landes, but in all the land of Egypt was bread.
41.55: At the length all the land of Egypt was affamished, and the people cryed to Pharaoh for bread. And Pharaoh said unto all the Egyptians, Goe to Joseph: what he sayth to you, doe ye.
41.56: When the famine was upon all the land, Joseph opened all places, wherein the store was, and sold unto the Egyptians: for the famine waxed sore in the land of Egypt.
41.57: And all countries came to Egypt to bye corn of Joseph, because the famine was sore in all landes.

42.1: Then Iaakob saw that there was food in Egypt, and Iaakob said unto his sonnes, Why gaze ye one upon an other?
42.2: And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is food in Egypt, Get you down thither, and bie us food thence, that we may live and not die.
42.3: So went Iosephs ten brethren down to bye corn of the Egyptians.
42.4: But Beniamin Iosephs brother would not Iaakob send with his brethren: for he said, Least death should befall him.
42.5: And the sonnes of Israel came to bye food among them that came: for there was famine in the land of Canaan.
42.6: Now Joseph was gouerner of the land, who sold to all the people of the land: then Iosephs brethren came, and bowed their face to the groud before him.
42.7: And when Joseph saw his brethren, hee knew them, and made himself straunge toward them, and spake to them roughly, and said unto them, Whence come yee? Who answered, Out of the land of Canaan, to bye vitaile.
42.8: (Now Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.
42.9: And Joseph remembred the dreames, which he dreamed of them) and he sayde unto them, Ye are spies, and are come to see the weakness of the land.
42.10: But they sayde unto him, Nay, my lord, but to bye vitayle thy servants are come.
42.11: Wee are all one mans sonnes: wee mean truely, and thy servants are no spies.
42.12: But he said unto them, Nay, but yee are come to see the weakenes of the land.
42.13: And they said, We thy servants are twelve brethren, the sonnes of one man in the land of Canaan: and behold, the yongest is this day with our father, and one is not.
42.14: Again Joseph sayde unto them, This is it that I spake unto you, saying, Ye are spies.
42.15: Hereby ye shall be proved: by the life of Pharaoh, ye shall not goe hence, except your yongest brother come hither.
42.16: Send one of you which may fet your brother, and ye shall be kept in prison, that your words may be proved, whether there bee trueth in you: or els by the life of Pharaoh ye are but spies.
42.17: So he put them in ward three dayes.
42.18: Then Joseph said unto them the third day, This do, and live: for I fear God.
42.19: If ye be true men, let one of your brethren be bound in your prison house, and goe ye, carie food for the famine of your houses:
42.20: But bring your yonger brother unto me, that your wordes may be tried, and that ye dye not: and they did so.
42.21: And they said one to another, We have verily sinned against our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear him: therefore is this trouble come upon us.
42.22: And Reuben answered them, saying, Warned I not you, saying, Sinne not against the child, and ye would not hear? and lo, his blood is now required.
42.23: (And they were not aware that Joseph vnderstoode them: for he spake unto them by an interpreter.)
42.24: Then he turned from them, and wept, and turned to them again, and communed with them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.
42.25: So Joseph commanded that they should fill their sackes with wheat, and put every mans money again in his sack, and give them vitaile for the journey: and thus did he unto them.
42.26: And they layed their vitaile upon their asses, and departed thence.
42.27: And as one of them opened his sack for to give his ass provender in the ynne, he espyed his money: for lo, it was in his sackes mouth.
42.28: Then he sayde unto his brethren, My money is restored: for loe, it is even in my sack. And their heart fayled them, and they were astonished, and sayde one to another, What is this, that God hath done unto us?
42.29: And they came unto Iaakob their father unto the land of Canaan, and told him all that had befallen them, saying,
42.30: The man, who is Lord of the land, spake roughly to us, and put us in prison as spyes of the countrey.
42.31: And we sayd unto him, We are true men, and are no spies.
42.32: We be twelve brethren, sonnes of our father: one is not, and the yongest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.
42.33: Then the Lord of the countrey sayde unto us, Hereby shall I know if ye be true men: Leave one of your brethren with me, and take food for the famine of your houses and depart,
42.34: And bring your yongest brother unto me, that I may know that ye are no spies, but true men: so will I deliver you your brother, and yee shall occupie in the land.
42.35: And as they emptied their sacks, behold, every mans bundel of money was in his sack: and when they and their father saw the bundels of their money, they were afrayde.
42.36: Then Iaakob their father said to them, Ye have robbed me of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Beniamin: all these things are against me.
42.37: Then Reuben answered his father, saying, Slay my two sonnes, if I bring him not to thee again: deliver him to mine hand, and I will bring him to thee again.
42.38: But he said, My sonne shall not go down with you: for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if death come unto him by the way which ye goe, then ye shall bring my gray head with sorow unto the grave.

43.1: Now great famine was in the land.
43.2: And when they had eaten up the vitaile, which they had brought from Egypt, their father sayd unto them, Turn again, and bye us a little food.
43.3: And Judah answered him, saying, The man charged us by an othe, saying, Never see my face, except your brother be with you.
43.4: If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will goe down, and bye thee food:
43.5: But if thou wilt not send him, we wil not go down: for the man said unto us, Look me not in the face, except your brother be with you.
43.6: And Israel sayd, Wherefore delt ye so evil with me, as to tell the man, whether ye had yet a brother or no?
43.7: And they answered, The man asked straitly of our selves and of our kinred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have ye any brother? And wee told him according to these wordes: could we know certainely that he would say, Bring your brother down?
43.8: Then sayde Judah to Israel his father, Send the boy with mee, that we may rise and goe, and that we may live and not dye, both we, and thou, and our children.
43.9: I wil be suertie for him: of mine hand shalt thou require him. If I bring him not to thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever.
43.10: For except we had made this tarying, doutlesse by this we had returned the second time.
43.11: Then their father Israel sayd unto them, If it must needes be so now, do thus: take of the best fruites of the land in your vessels, and bring the man a present, a little rosen, and a little hony, spices and myrrh, nuttes, and almondes:
43.12: And take double money in your hand, and the money, that was brought again in your sackes mouthes: cary it again in your hand, lest it were some oversight.
43.13: Take also your brother and arise, and go again to the man.
43.14: And God almightie give you mercie in the sight of the man, that hee may deliver you your other brother, and Beniamin: but I shall be robbed of my child, as I have been.
43.15: Thus the men took this present, and took twise so much money in their hand with Beniamin, and rose up, and went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.
43.16: And whe Joseph saw Beniamin with them, he sayde to his steward, Bring these men home and kill meat, and make ready: for the men shall eat with me at noon.
43.17: And the man did as Joseph bad, and brought the men unto Iosephs house.
43.18: Now when the men were brought into Iosephs house, they were afrayd, and sayd, Because of the money, that came in our sackes mouthes at the first time, are we brought, that hee may pick a quarrell against us, and lay some thing to our charge, and bring us in bondage and our asses.
43.19: Therefore came they to Iosephs steward, and communed with him at the door of ye house.
43.20: And said, Oh syr, we came in deed down hither at the first time to bye food,
43.21: And as wee came to an ynne and opened our sackes, behold, every mans money was in his sackes mouth, even our money in full weight, but we have brought it again in our handes.
43.22: Also other money have we brought in our handes to bye food, but we cannot tell, who put our money in our sackes.
43.23: And he said, Peace be unto you, fear not: your God and the God of your father hath given you that treasure in your sackes, I had your money: and he brought forth Simeon to them.
43.24: So the man led them into Iosephs house, and gave them water to wash their feet, and gave their asses provender.
43.25: And they made ready their present against Joseph came at noon, (for they heard say, that they should eat bread there)
43.26: When Joseph came home, they brought the present into the house to him, which was in their handes, and bowed down to the ground before him.
43.27: And he asked them of their prosperitie, and sayd, Is your father the old man, of whom ye told me, in good health? is he yet alive?
43.28: Who answered, Thy servant our father is in good health, he is yet alive: and they bowed down, and made obeysance.
43.29: And he lifting up his eyes, beheld his brother Beniamin his mothers sonne, and sayde, Is this your yonger brother, of whom ye told me? And he said, God be merciful unto thee, my son.
43.30: And Joseph made haste (for his affection was inflamed toward his brother, and sought where to weep) and entred into his chamber, and wept there.
43.31: Afterward he washed his face, and came out, and refrained himself, and sayd, Set on meat.
43.32: And they prepared for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves, because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Ebrewes: for that was an abomination unto the Egyptians.
43.33: So they sat before him: the eldest according unto his age, and the yongest according unto his youth. and the men marueiled among themselves.
43.34: And they took meases from before him, and sent to them: but Beniamins mease was five times so much as any of theirs: and they drunk, and had of the best drink with him.

44.1: Afterward he commanded his steward, saying, Fill the mens sackes with food, as much as they can carry, and put every mans money in his sackes mouth.
44.2: And put my cup, I mean the silver cup, in the sackes mouth of the yongest, and his corn money. And he did according to the commandement that Joseph gave him.
44.3: And in the morning the men were sent away, they, and their asses.
44.4: And when they went out of the citie not far off, Joseph sayd to his steward, Up, follow after the men: and when thou doest overtake them, say unto them, Wherefore have ye rewarded evil for good?
44.5: Is that not the cuppe, wherein my Lord drinketh? and in the which he doeth deuine and prophecie? ye have done evil in so doing.
44.6: And when he overtook them, he sayde those wordes unto them.
44.7: And they answered him, Wherefore sayeth my lord such wordes? God forbid that thy servants should do such a thing.
44.8: Behold, the money which we found in our sackes mouthes, wee brought again to thee out of the land of Canaan: how then should we steal out of thy lordes house silver or gold?
44.9: With whomesoeuer of thy servants it bee found, let him dye, and we also will be my lordes bondmen.
44.10: And he said, Now then let it be according unto your wordes: he with whom it is found, shall be my servant, and ye shalbe blameless.
44.11: Then at once every man took down his sack to the ground, and every one opened his sack.
44.12: And he searched, and began at the eldest and left at the yongest: and the cuppe was found in Beniamins sack.
44.13: Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and went again into the citie.
44.14: So Judah and his brethren came to Iosephs house (for he was yet there) and they fel before him on the ground.
44.15: Then Joseph sayd unto them, What act is this, which ye have done? know ye not that such a man as I, can deuine and prophecie?
44.16: Then sayd Judah, What shall we say unto my lord? what shall we speak? and how can we iustifie our selves? God hath found out the wickedness of thy servants: behold, we are servants to my Lord, both wee, and he, with whom the cuppe is found.
44.17: But he answered, God forbid, that I should doe so, but the man, with whom the cuppe is found, he shalbe my servant, and go ye in peace unto your father.
44.18: Then Judah drew neere unto him, and sayde, O my Lord, let thy servant now speak a word in my lordes eares, and let not thy wrath be kindled against thy servant: for thou art even as Pharaoh.
44.19: My Lord asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father, or a brother?
44.20: And we answered my Lord, We have a father that is old, and a young child, which he begat in his age: and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loveth him.
44.21: Now thou saidest unto thy servants, Bring him unto me, that I may set mine eye upon him.
44.22: And we answered my lord, The child can not depart from his father: for if he leave his father, his father would die.
44.23: Then saydest thou unto thy servants, Except your yonger brother come down with you, look in my face no more.
44.24: So when we came unto thy servant our father, and shewed him what my lord had sayd,
44.25: And our father sayde unto us, Goe again, bye us a litle food,
44.26: Then we answered, We can not go down: but if our yongest brother go with us, then will we go down: for we may not see the mans face, except our yongest brother be with us.
44.27: Then thy servant my father sayde unto us, Ye know that my wife bare me two sonnes,
44.28: And the one went out from me, and I said, Of a suretie he is torn in pieces, and I saw him not since.
44.29: Now yee take this also away from me: if death take him, then yee shall bring my gray head in sorowe to the grave.
44.30: Now therefore, when I come to thy servant my father, and the child be not with us (seeing that his life dependeth on the childes life)
44.31: Then when hee shall see that the child is not come, he will die: so shall thy servants bring the gray head of thy servant our father with sorowe to the grave.
44.32: Doubtless thy servant became suertie for the child to my father, and said, If I bring him not unto thee again, then I will bear the blame unto my father for ever.
44.33: Now therefore, I pray thee, let me thy servant bide for the child, as a servant to my Lord, and let the child go up with his brethren.
44.34: For how can I go up to my father, if the child be not with me, vnlesse I would see the evil that shall come on my father?

45.1: Then Joseph could not refrain him self before all that stood by him, but hee cryed, Have forth every man from me. And there taryed not one with him, while Joseph uttered himself unto his brethren.
45.2: And hee wept and cried, so that the Egyptians heard: the house of Pharaoh heard also.
45.3: Then Joseph sayde to his brethren, I am Joseph: doeth my father yet live? But his brethren could not answer him, for they were astonished at his presence.
45.4: Again, Joseph sayde to his brethren, Come neere, I pray you, to mee. And they came neere. And he sayde, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.
45.5: Now therefore be not sad, neither grieved with your selves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you for your preseruation.
45.6: For now two yeeres of famine have been through ye land, and five yeeres are behind, wherein neither shalbe earing nor harvest.
45.7: Wherefore God sent me before you to preserve your posteritie in this land, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.
45.8: Now the you sent not me hither, but God, who hath made mee a father unto Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.
45.9: Haste you and go up to my father, and tel him, Thus saieth thy sonne Joseph, God hath made me lord of all Egypt: come down to me, tary not.
45.10: And thou shalt dwel in ye land of Goshen, and shalt be neere me, thou and thy children, and thy childrens children, and thy sheep, and thy beastes, and all that thou hast.
45.11: Also I will nourish thee there (for yet remain five yeeres of famine) lest thou perish through pouertie, thou and thy houshold, and all that thou hast.
45.12: And behold, your eyes doe see, and the eyes of my brother Beniamin, that my mouth speaketh to you.
45.13: Therefore tel my father of al mine honour in Egypt, and of all that ye have seen, and make haste, and bring my father hither.
45.14: Then hee fell on his brother Beniamins neck, and wept, and Beniamin wept on his neck.
45.15: Moreover, he kissed all his brethren, and wept upon them: and afterward his brethren talked with him.
45.16: And the tidinges came unto Pharaohs house, so that they said, Iosephs brethre are come: and it pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.
45.17: Then Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Say to thy brethren, This doe ye, lade your beastes and depart, go to the land of Canaan,
45.18: And take your father, and your houshoulds, and come to me, and I wil give you the best of the land of Egypt, and ye shall eat of the fat of the land.
45.19: And I commaund thee, Thus doe ye, take you charets out of the land of Egypt for your children, and for your wives, and bring your father and come.
45.20: Also regard not your stuff: for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.
45.21: And the children of Israel did so: and Joseph gave them charets according to the commandement of Pharaoh: hee gave them vitaile also for the journey.
45.22: He gave them all, none except, change of raiment: but unto Beniamin he gave three hundreth pieces of silver, and five sutes of raiment.
45.23: And unto his father likewise hee sent ten hee asses laden with the best things of Egypt, and ten she asses laden with wheat, and bread and meat for his father by the way.
45.24: So sent he his brethren away, and they departed: and he sayde unto them, Fall not out by the way.
45.25: Then they went up from Egypt, and came unto the land of Canaan unto Iaakob their father,
45.26: And told him, saying, Joseph is yet alive, and he also is gouernour over all the land of Egypt, and Iaakobs heart failed: for he beleeued them not.
45.27: And they told him al the words of Joseph, which he had said unto the: but when he saw the charets, which Joseph had sent to cary him, then the spirit of Iaakob their father revived.
45.28: And Israel said, I have inough: Joseph my sonne is yet alive: I will go and see him yer I die.

46.1: Then Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beer-sheba, and offered sacrifice unto the God of his father Izhak.
46.2: And God spake unto Israel in a vision by night, saying, Iaakob, Iaakob. Who answered, I am here.
46.3: Then hee sayde, I am God, the God of thy father, fear not to goe down into Egypt: for I will there make of thee a great nation.
46.4: I wil go down with thee into Egypt, and I will also bring thee up again, and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.
46.5: Then Iaakob rose up from Beer-sheba: and the sonnes of Israel caried Iaakob their father, and their children, and their wives in the charets, which Pharaoh had sent to cary him.
46.6: And they took their cattell and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt, both Iaakob and all his seed with him,
46.7: His sonnes and his sonnes sonnes with him, his daughters and his sonnes daughters, and al his seed brought he with him into Egypt.
46.8: And these are the names of the children of Israel, which came into Egypt, even Iaakob and his sonnes: Reuben, Iaakobs first borne.
46.9: And the sonnes of Reuben: Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
46.10: And the sonnes of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar; and Shaul the sonne of a Canaanitish woman.
46.11: Also the sonnes of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
46.12: Also the sonnes of Judah: Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pharez, and Zerah: (but Er and Onan died in ye land of Canaan) And the sonnes of Pharez were Hezron and Hamul.
46.13: Also the sonnes of Issachar: Tola, and Phuuah, and Job, and Shimron.
46.14: Also the sonnes of Zebulun: Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
46.15: These bee the sonnes of Leah, which she bare unto Iaakob in Padan Aram, with his daughter Dinah. All the soules of his sonnes and his daughters were thirtie and three.
46.16: Also the sonnes of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
46.17: Also the sonnes of Asher: Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And the sonnes of Beriah: Heber, and Malchiel.
46.18: These are the children of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter: and these she bare unto Iaakob, even sixtene soules.
46.19: The sonnes of Rahel Iaakobs wife were Joseph and Beniamin.
46.20: And unto Joseph in the land of Egypt were borne Manasseh, and Ephraim, which Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah prince of On bare unto him.
46.21: Also the sonnes of Beniamin: Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
46.22: These are the sonnes of Rahel, which were borne unto Iaakob, fourteen soules in all.
46.23: Also the sonnes of Dan: Hushim.
46.24: Also the sonnes of Naphtali: Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
46.25: These are the sonnes of Bilhah, which Laban gave unto Rahel his daughter, and she bare these to Iaakob, in all, seven soules.
46.26: Al the soules, that came with Iaakob into Egypt, which came out of his loynes (beside Iaakobs sonnes wives) were in the whole, three score and six soules.
46.27: Also the sonnes of Joseph, which were borne him in Egypt, were two soules: so that al the soules of the house of Iaakob, which came into Egypt, are seuentie.
46.28: The he sent Judah before him unto Joseph, to direct his way unto Goshen, and they came into the land of Goshen.
46.29: Then Joseph made ready his charet and went up to Goshen to meet Israel his father, and presented himself unto him and fel on his neck, and wept upon his neck a good while.
46.30: And Israel sayde unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, and that thou art yet alive.
46.31: Then Joseph said to his brethren, and to his fathers house, I wil go up and shew Pharaoh, and tell him, My brethren and my fathers house, which were in the land of Canaan, are come unto me,
46.32: And the men are shepheardes, and because they are shepheardes, they have brought their sheep and their cattell, and all that they have.
46.33: And if Pharaoh call you, and ask you, What is your trade?
46.34: Then ye shall say, Thy servants are men occupied about cattell, from our childehood even unto this time, both we and our fathers: that yee may dwell in the land of Goshen: for every sheep keeper is an abomination unto the Egyptians.

47.1: Then came Joseph and told Pharaoh, and sayde, My father, and my brethren, and their sheep, and their cattell, and all that they have, are come out of the land of Canaan, and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.
47.2: And Joseph took part of his brethren, even five men, and presented them unto Pharaoh.
47.3: Then Pharaoh said unto his brethren, What is your trade? And they answered Pharaoh, Thy servants are shepheards, both we and our fathers.
47.4: They sayde moreover unto Pharaoh, For to soiourne in ye land are we come: for thy servants have no pasture for their sheep, so sore is ye famine in the land of Canaan. Now therefore, we pray thee, let thy servants dwel in the land of Goshen.
47.5: Then spake Pharaoh to Joseph, saying, Thy father and thy brethren are come unto thee.
47.6: The land of Egypt is before thee: in the best place of the land make thy father and thy brethren dwel: let the dwel in the land of Goshen: and if thou knowest that there be men of actiuitie among them, make them rulers over my cattell.
47.7: Joseph also brought Iaakob his father, and set him before Pharaoh. And Iaakob saluted Pharaoh.
47.8: Then Pharaoh sayde unto Iaakob, How old art thou?
47.9: And Iaakob sayd unto Pharaoh, The whole time of my pilgrimage is an hundreth and thirty yeeres: few and evil have the dayes of my life been, and I have not attayned unto the yeeres of the life of my fathers, in the dayes of their pilgrimages.
47.10: And Iaakob took leave of Pharaoh, and departed from the presence of Pharaoh.
47.11: And Joseph placed his father, and his brethren, and gave them possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, even in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
47.12: And Joseph nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his fathers houshold with bread, even to the yong children.
47.13: Now there was no bread in all the land: for the famine was exceeding sore: so that the land of Egypt, and the land of Canaan were famished by reason of the famine.
47.14: And Joseph gathered all the money, that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn which they bought, and Joseph layd up the money in Pharaohs house.
47.15: So when money fayled in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, then all the Egyptians came unto Joseph, and sayde, Give us bread: for why should we dye before thee? for our money is spent.
47.16: Then said Joseph, Bring your cattell, and I will give you for your cattell, if your money be spent.
47.17: So they brought their cattell unto Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread for the horses, and for the flockes of sheep, and for the heards of cattel, and for the asses: so he fed them with bread for all their cattell that yeere.
47.18: But when the yeere was ended, they came unto him the next yeere, and sayd unto him, We will not hide from my lord, that since our money is spent, and my lord hath the heards of the cattel, there is nothing left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies and our ground.
47.19: Why shall we perish in thy sight, both we, and our land? bye us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be bond to Pharaoh: therefore give us seed, that we may live and not dye, and that the land go not to waste.
47.20: So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh: for the Egyptians sold every man his ground because the famine was sore upon the: so the land became Pharaohs.
47.21: And he removed the people unto the cities, from one side of Egypt even to the other.
47.22: Onely the land of the Priestes bought he not: for the Priestes had an ordinarie of Pharaoh, and they did eat their ordinarie, which Pharaoh gave them: wherefore they sold not their ground.
47.23: Then Joseph sayd unto the people, Behold, I have bought you this day, and your land for Pharaoh: lo, here is seed for you: sow therefore the ground.
47.24: And of the encrease ye shall give the fifth part unto Pharaoh, and four partes shalbe yours for the seed of the field, and for your meat, and for them of your housholdes, and for your children to eat.
47.25: Then they answered, Thou hast saved our lives: let us find grace in the sight of my Lord, and we will be Pharaohs servants.
47.26: Then Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt unto this day, that Pharaoh should have the fift part, except the land of the priests only, which was not Pharaohs.
47.27: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the countrey of Goshen: and they had their possessions therein, and grew and multiplied exceedingly.
47.28: Moreover, Iaakob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen yeeres, so that the whole age of Iaakob was an hundreth fourtie and seven yeere.
47.29: Now when the time drew neere that Israel must dye, he called his sonne Joseph, and sayde unto him, If I have now found grace in thy sight, put thine hand now under my thigh, and deal mercifully and truely with me: burie me not, I pray thee, in Egypt.
47.30: But when I shall sleep with my fathers, thou shalt carry me out of Egypt, and bury mee in their buryall. And he answered, I will doe as thou hast sayde.
47.31: The he said, Swear unto me. And he sware unto him. And Israel worshipped towardes the beds head.

48.1: Again after this, one sayd to Joseph, Loe, thy father is sick: then hee took with him his two sonnes, Manasseh and Ephraim.
48.2: Also one told Iaakob, and said, Behold, thy sonne Joseph is come to thee, and Israel took his strength unto him and sat upon the bed.
48.3: Then Iaakob sayde unto Joseph, God almightie appeared unto me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me.
48.4: And he sayde unto me, Behold, I wil make thee fruitefull, and will multiplie thee, and will make a great number of people of thee, and will give this land unto thy seed after thee for an everlasting possession.
48.5: And now thy two sonnes, Manasseh and Ephraim, which are borne unto thee in the land of Egypt, before I came to thee into Egypt, shall be mine, as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
48.6: But the linage, which thou hast begotten after them, shalbe thine: they shall be called after the names of their brethren in their inheritance.
48.7: Now when I came from Padan, Rahel died upon mine hand in the land of Canaan, by the way when there was but half a dayes journey of ground to come to Ephrath: and I buryed her there in the way to Ephrath: the same is Beth-lehem.
48.8: Then Israel beheld Iosephs sonnes and sayd, Whose are these?
48.9: And Joseph sayd unto his father, They are my sonnes, which God hath given mee here. Then he sayd, I pray thee, bring them to me, that I may bless them:
48.10: (For the eyes of Israel were dimme for age, so that hee could not well see) Then he caused them to come to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
48.11: And Israel sayde unto Joseph, I had not thought to have seen thy face: yet lo, God hath shewed me also thy seed.
48.12: And Joseph took them away from his knees, and did reverence down to the ground.
48.13: Then took Joseph them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israels left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israels right hand, so he brought them unto him.
48.14: But Israel stretched out his right hand, and layde it on Ephraims head, which was the yonger, and his left hand upon Manassehs head (directing his handes of purpose) for Manasseh was the elder.
48.15: Also he blessed Joseph and sayde, The God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Izhak did walk, the God, which hath fed me al my life long unto this day, bless thee.
48.16: The Angel, which hath delivered me from all evil, bless the children, and let my name be named upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Izhak, that they may grow as fish into a multitude in the middes of the earth.
48.17: But when Joseph saw that his father layde his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he stayed his fathers hand to remooue it from Ephraims head to Manassehs head.
48.18: And Joseph sayde unto his father, Not so, my father, for this is the eldest: put thy right hand upon his head.
48.19: But his father refused, and sayd, I know well, my sonne, I know well: he shalbe also a people, and he shalbe great likewise: but his yonger brother shalbe greater then he, and his seed shall be full of nations.
48.20: So he blessed them that day, and sayde, In thee Israel shall bless, and say, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh. and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
48.21: Then Israel said unto Joseph, Behold, I die, and God shall be with you, and bring you again unto the land of your fathers.
48.22: Moreover, I have given unto thee one portion above thy brethren, which I gate out of the hand of the Amorite by my sword and by my bow.

49.1: Then Iaakob called his sonnes, and sayde, Gather your selves together, that I may tell you what shall come to you in the last dayes.
49.2: Gather your selves together, and hear, ye sonnes of Iaakob, and hearken unto Israel your father.
49.3: Reuben mine eldest sonne, thou art my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellencie of dignitie, and the excellencie of power:
49.4: Thou wast light as water: thou shalt not be excellent, because thou wentest up to thy fathers bed: then diddest thou defile my bed, thy dignitie is gone.
49.5: Simeon and Levi, brethren in evil, the instruments of crueltie are in their habitations.
49.6: Into their secret let not my soul come: my glory, be not thou ioyned with their assembly: for in their wrath they slew a man, and in their self will they digged down a wall.
49.7: Cursed be their wrath, for it was fierce, and their rage, for it was cruel: I will deuide them in Iaakob, and scatter them in Israel.
49.8: Thou Judah, thy brethre shall praise thee: thine hand shalbe in the neck of thine enemies: thy fathers sonnes shall bow down unto thee.
49.9: Judah, as a Lions whelp shalt thou come up from the spoyle, my sonne. He shall lye down and couch as a Lion, and as a Lioness: Who shall stirre him up?
49.10: The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor a Lawegiuer from between his feet, until Shiloh come, and the people shall be gathered unto him.
49.11: He shall bind his Ass foal unto ye vine, and his Asses colt unto the best vine. hee shall wash his garment in wine, and his cloke in the blood of grapes.
49.12: His eyes shalbe red with wine, and his teeth white with milk.
49.13: Zebulun shall dwell by the sea side, and he shalbe an haven for shippes: and his border shalbe unto Zidon.
49.14: Issachar shalbe a strong ass, couching down between two burdens:
49.15: And he shall see that rest is good, and that the land is pleasant, and he shall bow his shoulder to bear, and shalbe subiect unto tribute.
49.16: Dan shall judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel.
49.17: Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder by the path, byting the horse heeles, so that his rider shall fall backward.
49.18: O Lord, I have waited for thy salvation.
49.19: Gad, an host of men shall overcome him, but he shall overcome at the last.
49.20: Concerning Asher, his bread shalbe fat, and he shall give pleasures for a king.
49.21: Naphtali shalbe a hind let goe, giving goodly wordes.
49.22: Joseph shalbe a fruitefull bough, even a fruitful bough by the well side: the small boughs shall runne upon the wall.
49.23: And the archers grieved him, and shotte against him and hated him.
49.24: But his bow abode strong, and the hands of his armes were strengthened, by the handes of the mighty God of Iaakob, of whom was the feeder appointed, by the stone of Israel,
49.25: Even by the God of thy father, who shall help thee, and by the almightie, who shall bless thee with heavenly blessinges from above, with blessings of the deep, that lyeth beneath, with blessings of the brestes, and of the womb.
49.26: The blessings of thy father shalbe stronger then the blessings of mine elders: unto the end of the hilles of the world they shall be on the head of Joseph, and on the top of the head of him that was separate from his brethren.
49.27: Beniamin shall ravin as a wolf: in the morning he shall deuoure the pray, and at night he shall deuide the spoyle.
49.28: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and thus their father spake unto them, and blessed them: every one of them blessed hee with a several blessing.
49.29: And he charged them and sayd unto them, I am ready to be gathered unto my people: burie mee with my fathers in the cave, that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
49.30: In the cave that is in the field of Machpelah besides Mamre in the land of Canaan: which cave Abraham bought with the field of Ephron the Hittite for a possession to burie in.
49.31: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife: there they buryed Izhak and Rebekah his wife: and there I buried Leah.
49.32: The purchase of the field and the cave that is therein, was bought of the children of Heth.
49.33: Thus Iaakob made an end of giving charge to his sonnes, and plucked up his feet into the bed and gave up the ghost, and was gathered to his people.

50.1: Then Joseph fell upon his fathers face and wept upon him, and kissed him.
50.2: And Joseph commanded his seruantes the physicions, to enbaume his father, and the physicions enbaumed Israel.
50.3: So fourtie dayes were accomplished (for so long did the dayes of them that were enbaumed last) and the Egyptians bewayled him seuentie dayes.
50.4: And when the dayes of his mourning were past, Joseph spake to the house of Pharaoh, saying, If I have now found fauour in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the eares of Pharaoh, and say,
50.5: My father made me swear, saying, Loe, I die, bury me in my grave, which I have made me in the land of Canaan: now therefore let me go, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I wil come again.
50.6: Then Pharaoh said, Goe up and bury thy father, as he made thee to swear.
50.7: So Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went all the servants of Pharaoh, both the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt.
50.8: Likewise all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and his fathers house: onely their children, and their sheep, and their cattell left they in the land of Goshen.
50.9: And there went up with him both charets and horsemen: and they were an exceeding great company.
50.10: And they came to Goren Atad, which is beyond Iorden, and there they made a great and exceeding sore lamentation: and he mourned for his father seven dayes.
50.11: And when the Canaanites the inhabitants of the land saw the mourning in Goren Atad, they sayde, This is a great mourning unto the Egyptians: wherefore the name thereof was called Abel Mizraim, which is beyond Iorden.
50.12: So his sonnes did unto him, according as he had commanded them:
50.13: For his sonnes caried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which cave Abraham bought with the field, to be a place to bury in, of Ephron the Hittite besides Mamre.
50.14: Then Joseph returned into Egypt, he and his brethren, and al that went up with him to bury his father, after that he had buried his father.
50.15: And when Iosephs brethren saw that their father was dead, they sayde, It may be that Joseph will hate us, and will pay us again all the evil, which we did unto him.
50.16: Therefore they sent unto Joseph, saying, Thy father commanded before his death, saying,
50.17: Thus shall ye say unto Joseph, Forgive now, I pray thee, the trespass of thy brethren, and their sinne: for they rewarded thee evil. And now, we pray thee, forgive the trespass of the servants of thy fathers God. And Joseph wept, when they spake unto him.
50.18: Also his brethren came unto him, and fell down before his face, and sayde, Behold, we be thy servants.
50.19: To whom Joseph sayde, Fear not: for am not I under God?
50.20: When ye thought evil against mee, God disposed it to good, that he might bring to pass, as it is this day, and save much people alive.
50.21: Fear not now therefore, I will nourish you, and your children: and hee comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.
50.22: So Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he, and his fathers house: and Joseph lived an hundreth and tenne yeere.
50.23: And Joseph saw Ephraims children, even unto the third generation: also the sonnes of Machir the sonne of Manasseh were brought up on Iosephs knees.
50.24: And Joseph sayd unto his brethren, I am ready to dye, and God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land, unto ye land which hee sware unto Abraham, unto Izhak, and unto Iaakob.
50.25: And Joseph took an othe of the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall cary my bones hence.
50.26: So Joseph died, when he was an hundreth and ten yere old: and they enbaumed him and put him in a chest in Egypt.
